children.title: Standard-Form LP Representations
children.top_down_role: Equality-constrained nonnegative-variable presentations used by classical interior-point frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Form LP Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the equality-plus-nonnegativity convention for primal standard form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For data \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), a standard-form linear program and its dual are
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge 0\},\qquad \max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge 0\}.\]
Here \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(s\in\mathbb{R}^n\), while \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) is unrestricted. Inequalities involving \(x\) or \(s\) are componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard form minimizes a linear objective subject to equality constraints and nonnegative variables; its dual has unrestricted equality multipliers and nonnegative dual slacks.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) has dual \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).

source_refs.locator: 2 Background: Linear Programming and Interior-Point Methods p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x\) is primal feasible and \((y,s)\) is dual feasible, then \(c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=x^{\mathsf T}s\ge0\), and equality is equivalent to componentwise complementarity.

assumptions_latex: \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), and \(s\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c^{\mathsf T}x-b^{\mathsf T}y=x^{\mathsf T}s\ge0.

children.title: Canonical-Form LP Representations
children.top_down_role: Canonical sign conventions supporting primal or dual interior constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical-Form LP Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the maximization, upper-inequality, nonnegative-variable convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the canonical primal-dual pair is
\[\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\},\qquad \min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}.\]
All inequalities are componentwise. Reversing every objective and inequality sign gives the equivalent minimization-oriented convention; the convention must therefore be declared when “canonical form” is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated convention, canonical form is a maximization problem with upper inequalities and nonnegative variables, paired with a nonnegative covering-type dual.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b,\ x\ge0\}\) is paired with \(\min\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c,\ y\ge0\}\).

children.title: Inequality-Form LP Representations
children.top_down_role: Inequality-oriented presentations used in projective, barrier, or geometric treatments.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Form LP Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents an LP using affine inequalities and unrestricted primal variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), an inequality-form primal and its Lagrange dual are
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}z:Gz\ge h,\ z\in\mathbb{R}^n\},\qquad \max\{h^{\mathsf T}\lambda:G^{\mathsf T}\lambda=c,\ \lambda\ge0\}.\]
The variable \(z\) is unrestricted, and the inequalities are componentwise. Using constraints \(Gz\le h\) instead changes the sign convention for the dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality-form LP has unrestricted variables and affine inequalities; its dual uses nonnegative multipliers satisfying an equality involving the objective vector.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}z:Gz\ge h\}\) has dual \(\max\{h^{\mathsf T}\lambda:G^{\mathsf T}\lambda=c,\ \lambda\ge0\}\).

children.title: Cross-Form LP Conversions
children.top_down_role: Reformulations connecting the principal LP presentations while tracking interior structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Form LP Conversions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives finite-dimensional conversions preserving feasible objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Every finite-dimensional LP can be converted to equality-plus-nonnegativity form by the substitutions
\[Gz\le h\ \Longleftrightarrow\ Gz+u=h,\quad u\ge0,\qquad z_j=z_j^+-z_j^-,\quad z_j^+,z_j^-\ge0.\]
Conversely, an equality \(a^{\mathsf T}z=\beta\) is equivalent to the pair \(a^{\mathsf T}z\le\beta\) and \(-a^{\mathsf T}z\le-\beta\). These transformations preserve feasibility and objective values under the natural projection, although variable splitting need not give a one-to-one representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack variables replace inequalities, pairs of nonnegative variables replace free variables, and two opposite inequalities replace an equality while preserving projected feasible solutions and objectives.
assumptions_latex: The LP has finitely many real variables and linear equalities or inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed substitutions yield an equivalent LP under projection onto the original variables.

notation.meaning: nonnegative parts representing a free variable

source_refs.locator: 2 Background: Linear Programming and Interior-Point Methods p. 21

source_witnesses.locator: 2 Background: Linear Programming and Interior-Point Methods p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict Interiority Is Not Invariant Under Form Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes projected LP equivalence from preservation of positive-slack and logarithmic-barrier geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Gz\le h\), the slack conversion \(Gz+u=h\), \(u\ge0\), satisfies \(Gz<h\iff u=h-Gz>0\). In contrast, replacing \(a^{\mathsf T}z=\beta\) by \(a^{\mathsf T}z\le\beta\) and \(-a^{\mathsf T}z\le-\beta\) yields no feasible point at which both displayed inequalities are strict. The split representation \(z_j=z_j^+-z_j^-\), \(z_j^+,z_j^-\ge0\), has nonunique fibers and infinitely many strictly positive lifts of every scalar \(z_j\). Thus these transformations preserve projected feasible points and objective values but need not preserve positive-slack interiors or the logarithmic central path associated with a representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack introduction preserves strictness of a one-sided inequality, while equality duplication and free-variable splitting can change positive-slack and barrier geometry despite projected LP equivalence.
assumptions_latex: Strict inequality interior means positivity of every slack introduced for a displayed inequality; a logarithmic central path is defined using the displayed nonnegative variables or inequality slacks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Projected LP equivalence does not imply invariance of positive-slack interior or logarithmic-central-path geometry.}

notation.meaning: Nonnegative split variables representing one unrestricted coordinate.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Interiority Is Not Invariant Under Form Conversion

children.title: Strict Primal Interiority
children.top_down_role: Regimes with an interior primal feasible point irrespective of dual interior availability.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict primal interiority is equivalent to \(\exists x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) such that \(Ax=b\) and \(x>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict feasibility for the standard-form primal LP.

source_refs.locator: A Strictly Interior Point p. 29

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the standard-form primal feasible set \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), strict primal interiority holds precisely when
\[P^{\circ}_{+}:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ x>0\}\ne\varnothing.\]
Thus there exists an equality-feasible point whose every component is strictly positive. Whenever such a point exists, it is an interior point of \(P\) relative to the equality affine space \(\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b\}\). Strict primal interiority is stronger than merely requiring \(P\ne\varnothing\), and it does not assert that \(P\) has nonempty Euclidean interior in \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict primal interiority means that the equality constraints admit a feasible vector whose every component is positive; this is stronger than ordinary feasibility and does not require Euclidean interior in the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Primal Interiority

source_witnesses.locator: A Strictly Interior Point p. 29

children.title: Strict Dual Interiority
children.top_down_role: Regimes with an interior dual feasible point irrespective of primal interior availability.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Dual Interiority
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict feasibility of dual slacks for the standard-form primal-dual pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the dual feasible set \(D=\{(y,s):A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), strict dual interiority holds precisely when
\[D^{\circ}_{+}:=\{(y,s)\in\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^n:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s>0\}\ne\varnothing.\]
The multiplier \(y\) remains unrestricted; strictness applies only to the dual slack coordinates associated with primal nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict dual interiority means that the dual equality admits an unrestricted multiplier together with a componentwise positive dual slack.
assumptions_latex: \(D=\{(y,s):A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict dual interiority is equivalent to \(\exists(y,s)\) such that \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\) and \(s>0\).

notation.meaning: dual feasible set with strictly positive slack

children.title: Joint Primal-Dual Interiority
children.top_down_role: Two-sided interior regimes supporting feasible primal-dual trajectories.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Primal-Dual Interiority
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous strict feasibility of the standard-form primal and dual systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The standard-form primal-dual pair has joint primal-dual interiority when there exists \((x,y,s)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying
\[Ax=b,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\qquad x>0,\qquad s>0.\]
No complementarity equation is imposed: in particular, joint interiority is a strict-feasibility condition and is distinct from primal-dual optimality, which requires \(x_i s_i=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint interiority requires one strictly positive primal feasible vector and one dual feasible pair with strictly positive slack; it does not require complementarity.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual pair is in equality-plus-nonnegativity standard form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Joint interiority holds exactly when both strict primal interiority and strict dual interiority hold.

notation.meaning: primal variable, equality multiplier, and dual slack

children.title: Missing-Interiority Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where one or both feasible regions lack the interior required by feasible-start constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Missing-Interiority Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the usual positive-orthant barrier domain under mere feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Feasibility does not imply strict primal interiority. For example,
\[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:x_1+x_2=0,\ x\ge0\}=\{(0,0)\}.\]
Hence \(P\ne\varnothing\) but \(P^{\circ}_{+}=\varnothing\), so the logarithmic barrier \(-\sum_{i=1}^2\log x_i\) has no feasible domain. Analogously, if every dual feasible slack has some zero coordinate, strict dual interiority fails. Feasible-start methods requiring \(x>0\) and \(s>0\) then cannot be initialized without reformulation or an infeasible-start or embedding construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible LP may lie entirely on the nonnegative orthant’s boundary, leaving the logarithmic barrier domain empty and preventing strictly feasible initialization.
assumptions_latex: Strict feasibility is required in the original standard-form coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonempty primal or dual feasibility alone does not guarantee a strictly positive feasible point or a nonempty feasible logarithmic-barrier domain.

source_refs.locator: 6 Infeasible-Interior-Point Algorithms p. 107

source_witnesses.locator: 6 Infeasible-Interior-Point Algorithms p. 107

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certificates for a Forced Boundary Coordinate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite data-level certificates that a specified primal variable or dual slack is identically zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\ne\varnothing\). A coordinate \(x_j\) is zero for every \(x\in P\) if and only if there exists \(u\in\mathbb R^m\) such that
\[A^{\mathsf T}u\ge e_j,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}u=0.\]
Likewise, if the dual feasible set is nonempty, its slack coordinate \(s_j\) is always zero if and only if there exists \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) such that
\[Av=0,\qquad v\ge e_j,\qquad c^{\mathsf T}v=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear multiplier certificates verify that a chosen primal coordinate or dual slack is forced to the boundary throughout a nonempty feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The relevant primal or dual feasible set is nonempty.
\(e_j\) is the jth coordinate vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed multiplier systems are equivalent to the corresponding coordinate being identically zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificates for a Forced Boundary Coordinate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes missing strict interiority in a nonempty standard-form feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\ne\varnothing\). Then
\[P\cap\mathbb R_{++}^n\ne\varnothing\iff \forall i\ \exists x^{(i)}\in P:\ x_i^{(i)}>0.\]
Consequently,
\[P\cap\mathbb R_{++}^n=\varnothing\iff \exists j\ \forall x\in P:\ x_j=0.\]
For a nonempty dual feasible set, strict dual interiority fails analogously exactly when one slack coordinate is zero for every dual feasible pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty standard-form feasible set lacks a positive point exactly when some coordinate is forced to zero; the same holds for dual slacks.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\ne\varnothing\).
For the dual assertion, \(D=\{(y,s):A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\cap\mathbb R_{++}^n=\varnothing\iff\exists j\;\forall x\in P:\ x_j=0, with the analogous dual-slack equivalence.

notation.meaning: a feasible point with positive ith coordinate

knowledge_statements.title: Forced-Zero Characterization of Missing Interiority

children.title: Rank-Aware Reformulation Family
children.top_down_role: Constraint-system structure affecting path existence and Newton-system representations.

children.title: Full-Rank Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Constraint systems whose independent rows support standard local-system representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Rank Constraint Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-full-rank condition for standard-form equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a standard-form equality system \(Ax=b\) with \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), the constraint system is row-full-rank when
\[\operatorname{rank}(A)=m,\]
which necessarily requires \(m\le n\). Equivalently, the rows of \(A\) are linearly independent, \(AA^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite, and \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) implies \(y=0\). This condition concerns independence of equality constraints and does not itself imply feasibility or strict interiority.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint matrix is row-full-rank when all equality rows are independent; this makes its row Gram matrix positive definite but does not ensure feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\) if and only if \(AA^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).

children.title: Rank-Deficient Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Constraint systems requiring special treatment of dependent rows or singular reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Constraint Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detects dependent equality rows and consistency of their right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), the equality system \(Ax=b\) is row-rank-deficient when \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\). Its equations are consistent exactly when every row dependency is also satisfied by the right-hand side:
\[y^{\mathsf T}A=0\ \Longrightarrow\ y^{\mathsf T}b=0.\]
Equivalently, \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\). If this implication fails, the LP is infeasible; if it holds, dependent equations may be removed without changing the primal feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank deficiency means dependent equality rows. The system is consistent only when the right-hand side obeys every corresponding dependency.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\), consistency of \(Ax=b\) is equivalent to \(y^{\mathsf T}b=0\) for every \(y\) with \(y^{\mathsf T}A=0\).

notation.meaning: column space of the constraint matrix

children.top_down_role: Structural treatment of constraints that do not alter the feasible set.

assumptions_latex: Exact row-dependency decisions are available.
\(A_I\) spans the row space of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(b=Tb_I\), then \(\{x:Ax=b\}=\{x:A_Ix=b_I\}\); otherwise \(\{x:Ax=b\}=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Removes dependent equalities while detecting inconsistency.

source_refs.locator: 2 Background: Linear Programming and Interior-Point Methods p. 21

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), select row indices \(I\) such that \(A_I\) has full row rank and \(\operatorname{row}(A_I)=\operatorname{row}(A)\). Compute \(T\) satisfying \(A=TA_I\). If \(b\ne Tb_I\), declare \(Ax=b\) inconsistent. Otherwise replace \(Ax=b\) by \(A_Ix=b_I\). The reduced and original equality systems then have exactly the same solutions, so an LP with either system has the same feasible set and objective values at corresponding feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a basis of constraint rows, test whether the right-hand side satisfies the same dependencies, and either report inconsistency or discard redundant equations while preserving the feasible set and objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant-Constraint Handling

children.title: Interiority-Preserving Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent LP presentations assessed by their preservation of usable interior points.

knowledge_statements.title: Interiority-Preserving Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes affine coordinate changes preserving strict positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), and reformulate variables by \(x=Dz\), where \(D\) is a positive diagonal matrix. Then
\[Ax=b,\ x>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad ADz=b,\ z>0.\]
Consequently, positive diagonal scaling preserves strict primal interiority bijectively. Likewise, deleting consistent redundant equality rows preserves the set \(\{x:Ax=b,\ x>0\}\). By contrast, slack introduction or free-variable splitting changes the ambient orthant and need not preserve strict interiority without additional conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal scaling and deletion of consistent redundant equalities preserve strictly positive feasibility; slack introduction and variable splitting may not.
assumptions_latex: \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is diagonal with \(D_{ii}>0\).
Any deleted equality is implied by the retained equalities, including its right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and scaled systems have strictly positive feasible points simultaneously, and consistent redundant-row deletion leaves their set unchanged.

source_refs.locator: A Strictly Interior Point p. 29

source_witnesses.locator: A Strictly Interior Point p. 29

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the sharp boundary for preserving an interior after inequalities are converted to nonnegative slacks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For inequalities \(Gx\le h\), introduce \(u=h-Gx\ge0\). The reformulated system admits a feasible point with \(u>0\) exactly when the original inequalities admit a strictly feasible point:
\[\exists(x,u):Gx+u=h,\ u>0\iff\exists x:Gx<h.\]
Thus ordinary feasibility of \(Gx\le h\) does not suffice to preserve a nonempty positive-slack barrier domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack introduction yields positive slacks exactly when the original inequalities can all be satisfied strictly.
assumptions_latex: Inequalities are interpreted componentwise.
Any additional constraints on \(x\) are imposed identically in both formulations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists(x,u):Gx+u=h,\ u>0\iff\exists x:Gx<h.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Interiority Criterion for Slack Introduction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-Dual Interiority under Positive Monomial Variable Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends positive diagonal scaling to the exact class of linear orthant automorphisms, including coordinate permutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be a positive monomial matrix and set
\[x=Mz,\qquad \widetilde A=AM,\qquad \widetilde c=M^{\mathsf T}c,\qquad t=M^{\mathsf T}s.\]
Then the original standard-form pair corresponds bijectively to
\[\min\{\widetilde c^{\mathsf T}z:\widetilde A z=b,\ z\ge0\},\qquad \widetilde A^{\mathsf T}y+t=\widetilde c,\ t\ge0.\]
This correspondence preserves primal, dual, and joint strict interiority, objective values, and the complementarity pairing \(x^{\mathsf T}s=z^{\mathsf T}t\). Conversely, an invertible linear map carrying \(\mathbb R_+^n\) onto itself is monomial with positive nonzero entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive scalings and coordinate permutations are precisely the linear orthant automorphisms, and they preserve strict primal-dual feasibility and complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is monomial with one positive entry in each row and column.
The LP uses equality-plus-nonnegativity standard form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformation preserves primal, dual, and joint interiority and satisfies \(x^{\mathsf T}s=z^{\mathsf T}t\).
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Interiority under Positive Monomial Variable Transformations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Interiority Invariance under Invertible Row Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tracks primal and dual strict feasibility through an invertible recombination of equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) be nonsingular and replace \((A,b)\) by \((RA,Rb)\). Then the primal feasible set is unchanged. Moreover,
\[A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\iff (RA)^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+s=c,\qquad \widehat y=R^{-\mathsf T}y,\]
so the feasible slack set is unchanged and primal, dual, and joint interiority are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible row recombination preserves the primal feasible set and dual slack set while bijectively transforming equality multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \((A,b)\) by \((RA,Rb)\) preserves primal, dual, and joint interiority.
knowledge_statements.title: Interiority Invariance under Invertible Row Transformations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Joint Interiority under Consistent Redundant-Row Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extends the seed's primal statement to dual slacks and joint interiority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \((\bar A,\bar b)\) is obtained from \((A,b)\) by retaining an independent row subsystem and every deleted equality, including its right-hand side, is implied by the retained subsystem. Then
\[\{x:Ax=b\}=\{x:\bar A x=\bar b\},\qquad \operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})=\operatorname{range}(\bar A^{\mathsf T}).\]
Hence the primal feasible set and the set of attainable dual slacks \(\{s\ge0:c-s\in\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\}\) are unchanged. Strict primal, strict dual, and joint interiority are therefore preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting consistent redundant equalities preserves both the primal feasible set and the attainable dual slack set, hence all three interiority regimes.
assumptions_latex: Every deleted row and its right-hand-side entry are implied by the retained subsystem.
The retained rows span the row space of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistent redundant-row deletion preserves primal, dual, and joint interiority.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Interiority under Consistent Redundant-Row Deletion

children.title: Reformulation Effects on Central Trajectories

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Redundant-Equality Deletion Preserves the Primal-Slack Central Trajectory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of deleting consistent dependent equality rows while retaining the same barrier variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=TA_I\) and \(b=Tb_I\), where \(A_I\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) has full row rank and spans \(\operatorname{row}(A)\). For every \(\mu>0\), the systems \[Ax=b,\quad A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\quad XSe=\mu e,\quad x,s>0\] and \[A_Ix=b_I,\quad A_I^{\mathsf T}y_I+s=c,\quad XSe=\mu e,\quad x,s>0\] have exactly the same \((x,s)\)-solutions. The associated multipliers satisfy \(y_I=T^{\mathsf T}y\); the multiplier \(y\) for the unreduced system can be nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting consistent dependent equality rows leaves the primal variables and dual slacks on the central path unchanged, although the redundant multiplier representation can be nonunique.
assumptions_latex: \(A=TA_I\) and \(b=Tb_I\).
\(A_I\) has full row rank and spans \(\operatorname{row}(A)\).
The two formulations use the same positive variables \(x,s\) and parameter \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(x,s):\exists y\text{ satisfying the full central system}\}=\{(x,s):\exists y_I\text{ satisfying the reduced central system}\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Barrier-Variable Duplication Changes the Projected Central Trajectory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent projected feasible sets whose equal-weight logarithmic barriers select different projected central points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the zero-objective formulations \(x+s=1\), \(x,s>0\), and \(x+s_1+s_2=1\), \(x,s_1,s_2>0\). Both project onto \(0<x<1\). The respective logarithmic-barrier minimizers satisfy \(x=s=1/2\) and \(x=s_1=s_2=1/3\). Hence their projected central trajectories are \(x(\mu)=1/2\) and \(x(\mu)=1/3\) for every \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting one positive slack into two equally barred positive variables preserves the projected feasible interval but changes the projected central trajectory from one half to one third.
assumptions_latex: The objective is identically zero.
Every displayed positive variable has a unit-weight logarithmic barrier.
Central points are the unique barrier minimizers on the displayed equality slices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x\mathcal C_1(\mu)=\{1/2\}\ne\{1/3\}=\operatorname{proj}_x\mathcal C_2(\mu)\quad(\mu>0).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Objective Scaling Reparameterizes the Central Trajectory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of multiplying the objective by a positive scalar while retaining the feasible set and barrier variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha>0\), let \(x_c(\mu)\) minimize \(c^{\mathsf T}x-\mu\sum_i\log x_i\) over \(Ax=b,\ x>0\), and let \(x_{\alpha c}(\mu)\) use objective \(\alpha c\). Then \[x_{\alpha c}(\mu)=x_c(\mu/\alpha).\] In coupled coordinates, if \((x,y,s)\) lies on the path for \(c\) at parameter \(\mu/\alpha\), then \((x,\alpha y,\alpha s)\) lies on the path for \(\alpha c\) at parameter \(\mu\). Thus positive objective scaling preserves the primal trajectory as an unparameterized curve but rescales its parameter and dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying the objective by a positive constant leaves the primal central curve unchanged while rescaling the parameter and dual variables.
assumptions_latex: \alpha>0.
The primal and dual problems are strictly feasible.
Both formulations use the same equality system and positive barrier variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{\alpha c}(\mu)=x_c(\mu/\alpha),\qquad (y_{\alpha c}(\mu),s_{\alpha c}(\mu))=\alpha(y_c(\mu/\alpha),s_c(\mu/\alpha)).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equality-Row-Space Objective Shifts Preserve the Primal-Slack Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central-trajectory covariance when the objective is changed by a linear combination of equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the feasible set \(Ax=b\), replace \(c\) by \(c'=c+A^{\mathsf T}q\). The primal barrier objective changes by the constant \(q^{\mathsf T}b\), so its minimizer is unchanged for every \(\mu>0\). In coupled coordinates, \((x(\mu),y(\mu),s(\mu))\) for \(c\) maps to \((x(\mu),y(\mu)+q,s(\mu))\) for \(c'\). Thus the primal and slack trajectories are identical and only the equality multiplier is translated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a combination of equality rows to the objective leaves the primal central points and dual slacks unchanged while translating the equality multiplier.
assumptions_latex: Ax=b\text{ is the common equality system}.
c'=c+A^{\mathsf T}q.
The central path exists for the parameters under consideration.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular row transformation \(A_R=RA\), \(b_R=Rb\), and a positive diagonal variable scaling \(x=Dz\), set \(A_D=AD\), \(c_D=Dc\). Then the original central equations correspond exactly to the transformed equations through \(z=D^{-1}x\), \(s_z=Ds\), and \(y_R=R^{-\mathsf T}y\), because \(z_i(s_z)_i=x_i s_i=\mu\). Consequently, invertible row operations preserve the \((x,s)\)-trajectory, while positive diagonal scaling maps it bijectively. Reformulations introducing or eliminating barrier variables need not preserve the projected trajectory because they change the logarithmic barrier.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Solution Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard-form primal and dual optimal sets, including their cross-complementarity relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(X^*:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax=b,\ x\ge0,\ c^{\mathsf T}x=v^*\}\) and \(D^*:=\{(y,s)\in\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^n:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y=v^*\}\). These sets are convex faces of their respective feasible polyhedra. Every \(x\in X^*\) and \((y,s)\in D^*\) satisfy \(x^{\mathsf T}s=0\), equivalently \(x_i s_i=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal and dual solution sets are the feasible optimal faces, and every primal optimum is componentwise complementary to every dual optimal slack.
assumptions_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\).
Both programs attain a common finite optimal value \(v^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in X^*\) and \((y,s)\in D^*\), \(x^{\mathsf T}s=0\), equivalently \(x_i s_i=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Central-Path Partition Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic identification by the exact central path, not a finite-parameter or finite-precision threshold guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x(\mu),y(\mu),s(\mu))\) satisfy \(Ax(\mu)=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y(\mu)+s(\mu)=c\), and \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(x(\mu),s(\mu)>0\). As \(\mu\downarrow0\), the path converges to a strictly complementary optimal pair in the relative interiors of the optimal primal and slack faces. For \(i\in B\), \(x_i(\mu)\) has a positive limit and \(s_i(\mu)\to0\); for \(i\in N\), \(x_i(\mu)\to0\) and \(s_i(\mu)\) has a positive limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact central path identifies the optimal partition asymptotically: primal coordinates have positive limits on B, while dual slacks have positive limits on N.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank, and strictly feasible primal and dual points exist.
The common optimal value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limiting supports satisfy \(B=\{i:\lim_{\mu\downarrow0}x_i(\mu)>0\}\) and \(N=\{i:\lim_{\mu\downarrow0}s_i(\mu)>0\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Complementarity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise degeneracy can occur even though a strictly complementary optimal pair exists globally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(D_0(x^*,s^*):=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}:x_i^*=0\text{ and }s_i^*=0\}\). An optimal complementary pair is strictly complementary exactly when \(D_0(x^*,s^*)=\varnothing\). If \(D_0(x^*,s^*)\ne\varnothing\), the pair lies on a degenerate complementarity boundary, and the support of that pair need not identify the global optimal partition. Such pairwise degeneracy may occur even when the problem possesses another strictly complementary optimal pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimal pair is on a degenerate complementarity boundary when some primal variable and its matching slack both vanish; that pair's support need not identify the global optimal partition.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\in X^*\) and \((y^*,s^*)\in D^*\) form an optimal complementary pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair is strictly complementary exactly when \(D_0(x^*,s^*)=\varnothing\); otherwise it lies on a degenerate complementarity boundary.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed \(\mu>0\), let \(x(\mu)\) minimize the primal barrier objective \(\phi_\mu\), and let \((y(\mu),s(\mu))\) maximize the dual barrier objective \(\psi_\mu\). Their first-order optimality conditions coincide with \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), and \(XSe=\mu e\), with \(x,s>0\). Conversely, every positive solution of these equations satisfies the optimality conditions of both barrier problems. Thus all three orientations parameterize the same central triple, and their objective values satisfy \(\phi_\mu(x(\mu))-\psi_\mu(y(\mu),s(\mu))=n\mu-\mu\sum_i\log(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a common parameter, primal-barrier, dual-barrier, and perturbed-KKT formulations determine the same central triple through identical optimality conditions.

children.title: Primal Central-Path Parameterizations
children.top_down_role: Central trajectories expressed through primal barrier solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Central-Path Parameterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic-barrier parameterization of the standard-form primal LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). Consider \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), and suppose the primal and dual systems are strictly feasible. For every \(\mu>0\), the primal central-path point is the unique minimizer \[x(\mu)=\mathop{\arg\min}_{Ax=b,\,x>0}\left(c^Tx-\mu\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\right).\] Equivalently, there exist \(y(\mu)\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(s(\mu)\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) satisfying \(A^Ty(\mu)+s(\mu)=c\) and \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). With \(t=1/\mu\), the same point minimizes \(t c^Tx-\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\) over \(Ax=b\), \(x>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict primal and dual feasibility, each positive barrier parameter determines a unique primal logarithmic-barrier minimizer; its optimality conditions give the coupled complementarity equations, and the reciprocal parameter gives the equivalent scaled formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
There exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) with \(A\bar x=b\).
There exist \(\bar y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\bar s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) with \(A^T\bar y+\bar s=c\).
\(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x(\mu)=\mathop{\arg\min}_{Ax=b,\,x>0}\left(c^Tx-\mu\sum_{i=1}^n\log x_i\right).\]

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Central-Path Parameterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic-barrier parameterization of the standard-form dual LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For the dual problem \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), the dual central-path pair for each \(\mu>0\) is the unique maximizer \[(y(\mu),s(\mu))=\mathop{\arg\max}_{A^Ty+s=c,\,s>0}\left(b^Ty+\mu\sum_{i=1}^n\log s_i\right).\] Its first-order conditions provide \(x(\mu)\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) such that \(Ax(\mu)=b\) and \(x_i(\mu)s_i(\mu)=\mu\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Thus this dual barrier parameterization generates the same coupled central path as the primal barrier parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict primal and dual feasibility and full row rank, each positive barrier parameter determines a unique dual logarithmic-barrier maximizer whose optimality conditions give the same coupled primal-dual central path.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
There exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) with \(A\bar x=b\).
There exist \(\bar y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\bar s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) with \(A^T\bar y+\bar s=c\).
\(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(y(\mu),s(\mu))=\mathop{\arg\max}_{A^Ty+s=c,\,s>0}\left(b^Ty+\mu\sum_{i=1}^n\log s_i\right).\]

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Primal-Dual Parameterizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbed KKT representation of the standard primal-dual central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\). For each \(\mu>0\), the coupled primal-dual central-path point \((x(\mu),y(\mu),s(\mu))\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\times\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R_{++}^n\) is characterized by \[Ax(\mu)=b,\qquad A^Ty(\mu)+s(\mu)=c,\qquad X(\mu)S(\mu)e=\mu e.\] Here \(X(\mu)=\operatorname{Diag}(x(\mu))\), \(S(\mu)=\operatorname{Diag}(s(\mu))\), and \(e\in\mathbb R^n\) is the all-ones vector. Consequently, \(x(\mu)^Ts(\mu)=n\mu\), so the primal-dual gap is \(n\mu\), and every complementarity product equals \(\mu\). The system is the first-order optimality system of both logarithmic-barrier formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly feasible standard-form primal-dual LP, the coupled central path is represented by primal feasibility, dual feasibility, positivity, and equal perturbed complementarity products; its duality gap equals the dimension times the barrier parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\).
There exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) with \(A\bar x=b\).
There exist \(\bar y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\bar s\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) with \(A^T\bar y+\bar s=c\).
\(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[Ax=b,\qquad A^Ty+s=c,\qquad XSe=\mu e,\qquad x>0,\quad s>0.\]

children.title: Weighted Central-Path Parameterizations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for a genuinely interior weighted logarithmic central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the weighted coupled system \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(x_is_i=\mu w_i\), with \(x,s>0\) and \(\mu>0\), every weight must satisfy \(w_i>0\). If \(w_j=0\), the equation \(x_js_j=0\) is incompatible with strict positivity. If \(w_j<0\), it is incompatible with \(x_js_j>0\). Thus nonpositive weights do not define a strictly interior weighted central path of this form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive primal and dual variables force every weighted complementarity target to have a positive weight.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i>0\) and \(s_i>0\) for every \(i\).
\(x_is_i=\mu w_i\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\); any coordinate with \(w_i\le0\) is incompatible with the strictly interior coupled system.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Weight Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy between common rescaling of the weights and the path parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) and \(\alpha>0\), the weighted complementarity systems \(x_is_i=\mu(\alpha w_i)\) and \(x_is_i=(\alpha\mu)w_i\) are identical. Equivalently, the weighted barrier objectives with pairs \((\mu,\alpha w)\) and \((\alpha\mu,w)\) coincide. Consequently, a common positive scaling of all weights only reparameterizes the same trajectory, and one may normalize, for example, \(\sum_iw_i=n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling all weights by a common positive factor only rescales the path parameter, so weighted paths may be normalized without changing their trajectory.
assumptions_latex: \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
\(\alpha>0\) and \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C_{\alpha w}(\mu)=\mathcal C_w(\alpha\mu)\), so common weight scaling is a reparameterization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Analytic-Center Limit on the Optimal Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit selected by a fixed positive weight vector along the weighted primal logarithmic central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with strict primal and dual feasibility and finite optimum, and fix \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). Let \(x_w(\mu)\) minimize \(c^{\mathsf T}x-\mu\sum_i w_i\log x_i\) over \(Ax=b,\ x>0\). If \(F^*\) is the primal optimal face and \(B=\{i:\exists x\in F^*,\ x_i>0\}\), then \(x_w(\mu)\) converges as \(\mu\downarrow0\) to the unique maximizer \[x_w^*=\mathop{\arg\max}_{x\in\operatorname{relint}F^*}\sum_{i\in B}w_i\log x_i.\] Thus relative weights, unlike their common scale, determine the weighted analytic center selected on the optimal face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted central path converges to the weighted logarithmic analytic center of the primal optimal face; relative weights can change the selected limit.
assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal and dual LPs are strictly feasible.
The primal optimal value is finite.
\(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) is fixed while \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_w(\mu)\to x_w^*=\arg\max_{x\in\operatorname{relint}F^*}\sum_{i\in B}w_i\log x_i.

weighted analytic center of the optimal face

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual logarithmic-barrier formulation of the fixed-positive-weight central trajectory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and its dual \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\). Fix \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). For \(\mu>0\), let \((y_w(\mu),s_w(\mu))\) maximize \[b^{\mathsf T}y+\mu\sum_{i=1}^n w_i\log s_i\] subject to \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\) and \(s>0\). Its stationarity equations define \(x_{w,i}=\mu w_i/s_{w,i}\) and give \(Ax_w=b\). Hence the dual barrier produces the coupled weighted equations \(x_{w,i}s_{w,i}=\mu w_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using the same positive weights in the dual slack barrier yields the weighted coupled path, with each primal variable equal to its weighted target divided by its slack.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence, Uniqueness, and Analyticity of the Fixed-Weight Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity of the weighted central trajectory for a fixed strictly positive weight vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, suppose the standard-form primal and dual LPs are strictly feasible, and fix \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). For every \(\mu>0\), the weighted logarithmic-barrier problem has a unique minimizer \(x_w(\mu)\), and the weighted central equations determine unique \(y_w(\mu)\) and \(s_w(\mu)\). Moreover, \(\mu\mapsto(x_w(\mu),y_w(\mu),s_w(\mu))\) is real analytic on \((0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For fixed positive weights and a full-row-rank strictly feasible LP, every positive parameter has a unique weighted central point that varies analytically with the parameter.

\{x:Ax=b,\ x>0\}\ne\varnothing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relative Weights Change the Central Point on a Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes changes in relative weights from harmless common rescaling of every weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the zero-objective simplex \(\{x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n:e^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\), the weighted barrier point maximizes \(\sum_{i=1}^n w_i\log x_i\), where \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). Its unique value is \(x_i=w_i/W\), with \(W=\sum_jw_j\). Hence positive weight vectors that are not scalar multiples generally select different central points, whereas replacing \(w\) by \(\alpha w\), \(\alpha>0\), leaves the point unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a zero-objective simplex, the weighted central point is the normalized weight vector, so relative weights genuinely change the selected point.

\(e^{\mathsf T}x=1\) and \(x>0\).
The objective is zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(w\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). knowledge_statements.title: Central-Path Neighborhood Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard narrow, infinity-norm, and wide neighborhoods for feasible primal-dual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a strictly feasible triple \((x,y,s)\), set \(\mu=x^Ts/n\). For \(0<\theta<1\), the Euclidean and infinity-norm neighborhoods are \[\mathcal N_2(\theta)=\{(x,y,s):Ax=b,\ A^Ty+s=c,\ x,s>0,\ \|XSe-\mu e\|_2\le\theta\mu\},\] \[\mathcal N_\infty(\theta)=\{(x,y,s):Ax=b,\ A^Ty+s=c,\ x,s>0,\ \|XSe-\mu e\|_\infty\le\theta\mu\}.\] For \(0<\gamma<1\), a wide neighborhood is \(\mathcal N^-_\infty(\gamma)=\{(x,y,s):Ax=b,\ A^Ty+s=c,\ x,s>0,\ x_is_i\ge\gamma\mu\ \forall i\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Central-path neighborhoods bound complementarity deviations using Euclidean or infinity norms, while wide neighborhoods impose only coordinatewise lower bounds.

\(0<\theta<1\) and \(0<\gamma<1\).

If a point belongs to \(\mathcal N^-_\infty(\gamma)\), then \[\gamma\mu\le x_is_i\le\bigl(n-(n-1)\gamma\bigr)\mu\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).\]

knowledge_statements.title: Central-Path Endpoint Centers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of the unweighted central path at the optimal endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\) be the indices positive at some primal optimum and \(N\) the indices having positive slack at some dual optimum. As \(\mu\downarrow0\), the central path converges to \((x^*,y^*,s^*)\), where \(x^*\) is the unique maximizer of \(\sum_{i\in B}\log x_i\) over the relative interior of the primal optimal face, and \((y^*,s^*)\) is the unique maximizer of \(\sum_{i\in N}\log s_i\) over the relative interior of the dual optimal face. Thus the endpoint is the pair of analytic centers of the optimal faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The central path approaches the analytic centers of the primal and dual optimal faces as the barrier parameter tends to zero.

Their optimal solution sets are nonempty and bounded in the relevant faces.
The unweighted logarithmic central path is used.

knowledge_statements.title: Limiting Optimal Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal partition selected by vanishing central-path complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(B=\{i:\exists\,x\text{ primal optimal with }x_i>0\}\) and \(N=\{i:\exists\,(y,s)\text{ dual optimal with }s_i>0\}\). Then \(B\cap N=\varnothing\), and strict complementarity gives \(B\cup N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\). children.title: Central-Path Curvature Geometry
children.top_down_role: Second-order bending behavior of the central trajectory.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second derivative and Euclidean curvature of the full primal-dual central path parameterized by the barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z(\mu)=(x(\mu),y(\mu),s(\mu))\) be the full primal-dual central path. Its acceleration is the unique solution of \[A\ddot x=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}\ddot y+\ddot s=0,\qquad S\ddot x+X\ddot s=-2(\dot x\circ\dot s).\] Thus the tangent and acceleration use the same primal-dual Jacobian. For the Euclidean embedding \(z=(x,y,s)\), if \(\dot z\ne0\), the curvature is \[\kappa(\mu)=\frac{\left\|\left(I-\frac{\dot z\dot z^{\mathsf T}}{\|\dot z\|^2}\right)\ddot z\right\|}{\|\dot z\|^2}.\] This numerical curvature depends on the chosen coordinate embedding and metric, although it is invariant under regular reparameterization of that fixed embedded curve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Central-path acceleration solves the same primal-dual linearization as the tangent, and its component normal to the tangent determines Euclidean curvature for a specified embedding.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank and the primal and dual standard-form problems are strictly feasible.
\(\mu>0\), so the central path is twice differentiable and \(x(\mu),s(\mu)>0\).

children.title: Higher-Order Path Geometry

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative recursion of orders three and higher, beyond the tangent and curvature cases owned by sibling leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an integer \(r\ge3\). If the central path is \(r\)-times differentiable at \(\mu>0\), then \[Ax^{(r)}=0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y^{(r)}+s^{(r)}=0,\] and repeated differentiation of \(x\circ s=\mu e\) gives \[Sx^{(r)}+Xs^{(r)}=-\sum_{j=1}^{r-1}\binom{r}{j}x^{(j)}\circ s^{(r-j)}.\] Consequently the order-r derivative is obtained from the same primal-dual Jacobian as the tangent and acceleration, with a right-hand side determined entirely by lower-order derivatives. Under full row rank and positivity the full order-r derivative triple is unique; with redundant equality rows, multiplier derivatives can be nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every central-path derivative of order at least three solves the same primal-dual linearization with a right-hand side assembled from lower-order derivatives.
assumptions_latex: \(r\ge3\) is a fixed integer.
\(A\) has full row rank and the primal and dual standard-form problems are strictly feasible.
The central path is \(r\)-times differentiable at the chosen \(\mu>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Higher-Order Central-Path Derivatives
Higher-Order Path Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive derivative equations for all smooth orders of the central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the central path is \(k\)-times differentiable at \(\mu>0\). For every integer \(k\ge1\), its derivatives satisfy \[Ax^{(k)}=0,\qquad A^Ty^{(k)}+s^{(k)}=0,\qquad \sum_{j=0}^{k}\binom{k}{j}x^{(j)}\circ s^{(k-j)}=\delta_{k1}e.\] Isolating the terms \(j=0\) and \(j=k\) yields a linear system with coefficient blocks \(S\) and \(X\); its right-hand side depends only on lower-order derivatives. Hence all higher jets are generated recursively from the same primal-dual linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every higher derivative of the central path solves the same linearized feasibility system with a right-hand side built from lower derivatives.
assumptions_latex: The central path is \(k\)-times differentiable at the chosen positive parameter.
The primal-dual Newton system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Sx^{(k)}+Xs^{(k)}=\delta_{k1}e-\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}\binom{k}{j}x^{(j)}\circ s^{(k-j)}\), together with homogeneous feasibility derivatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Full Primal-Dual Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unreduced Newton system for a standard-form primal-dual LP pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal problem \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and dual problem \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\). At \(x,s>0\), a primal-dual Newton direction with prescribed complementarity right-hand side \(r_c\) is represented by \[\begin{pmatrix}0&A^T&I\\ A&0&0\\ S&0&X\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\Delta x\\ \Delta y\\ \Delta s\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_d\\ r_p\\ r_c\end{pmatrix},\] where \(r_p=b-Ax\) and \(r_d=c-A^Ty-s\). The rows are respectively the linearized dual-feasibility, primal-feasibility, and complementarity equations.

x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n

If \(A^Ty=0\) for some \(y\ne0\), then \((0,y,0)\in\ker M\).

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented Primal-Dual Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block system obtained by eliminating the slack direction from the full Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the full primal-dual system, assume \(x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), set \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and define \(H=X^{-1}S\). Eliminating \(\Delta s\) from \(A^T\Delta y+\Delta s=r_d\) and \(S\Delta x+X\Delta s=r_c\) gives the symmetric augmented system \[\begin{pmatrix}-H&A^T\\ A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}\Delta x\\ \Delta y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}r_d-X^{-1}r_c\\ r_p\end{pmatrix}.\] After solving it, recover the eliminated direction from \(\Delta s=r_d-A^T\Delta y\). Thus this augmented representation is algebraically equivalent to the full system whenever \(X\) is invertible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the slack direction yields an equivalent symmetric two-block augmented system, after which the slack direction is recovered from the dual-feasibility equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The augmented matrix has a fixed inertia under full row rank and is singular under dependent constraint rows.
assumptions_latex: H\succ0
A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}(A)=m\Longrightarrow\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(m,n,0)

notation.meaning: Numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues.

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is the augmented equations, their derivation by slack elimination, and slack recovery. The proposed inertia record is deferred because the Augmented-System Factorization leaf is the canonical home for symmetric-indefinite structure. Full-system organization, normal equations, correspondence, and numerical factorization remain excluded to their dedicated leaves.

children.title: Normal-Equation Systems
children.top_down_role: Further reduced local systems expressed in normal-equation form.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite Schur-complement reduction in the dual direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=X^{-1}S\) and \(q=X^{-1}r_c-r_d\). From the augmented equations \(H\Delta x-A^T\Delta y=q\) and \(A\Delta x=r_p\), elimination of \(\Delta x\) yields \[(AH^{-1}A^T)\Delta y=r_p-AH^{-1}q.\] If \(A\) has full row rank and \(x,s>0\), then \(AH^{-1}A^T\) is symmetric positive definite, so \(\Delta y\) is unique. The remaining directions are recovered by \(\Delta x=H^{-1}(q+A^T\Delta y)\) and \(\Delta s=r_d-A^T\Delta y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal direction produces symmetric positive-definite normal equations when the constraint matrix has full row rank.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\text{ has full row rank}
x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AH^{-1}A^T\succ0

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solvability and nonuniqueness of normal equations when equality rows are dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(H\succ0\), let \(N=AH^{-1}A^T\). Then \[N\succeq0,\qquad \ker N=\ker A^T,\qquad \operatorname{range}(N)=\operatorname{range}(A).\] Hence \(N\) is positive definite exactly when \(A\) has full row rank. If \(A\) is rank deficient, \(N\Delta y=g\) is solvable exactly when \(g\in\operatorname{range}(A)\), and its solutions are nonunique modulo \(\ker A^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted normal equations are singular exactly for dependent constraint rows; a singular system is solvable precisely for right-hand sides in the constraint range.
assumptions_latex: H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n},\ H\succ0
A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N\succ0\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{rank}(A)=m

children.title: Local-System Reduction Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Equivalence, recoverability, plus structural tradeoffs across coupled or reduced systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-System Reduction Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact solution correspondence among full, augmented, and normal-equation representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(x,s>0\) and that \(A\) has full row rank. A triple \((\Delta x,\Delta y,\Delta s)\) solves the full primal-dual Newton system if and only if \((\Delta x,\Delta y)\) solves its augmented system and \(\Delta s=r_d-A^T\Delta y\). Equivalently, \(\Delta y\) solves the normal equations, \(\Delta x=H^{-1}(X^{-1}r_c-r_d+A^T\Delta y)\), and \(\Delta s=r_d-A^T\Delta y\), where \(H=X^{-1}S\). Hence exact elimination and back-substitution establish a bijection between the solution sets; the representations differ computationally but not algebraically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact elimination and back-substitution give the same Newton direction in the full, augmented, and normal-equation formulations.
assumptions_latex: x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n
A\text{ has full row rank}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{full}}\leftrightarrow\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{augmented}}\leftrightarrow\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{normal}}

notation.meaning: Solution set of the indicated linear-system representation.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of exact reduction correspondence to compatible singular systems, including multiplier ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succ0\), \(N=AH^{-1}A^T\), and suppose the normal-equation right-hand side \(g\) lies in \(\operatorname{range}(A)=\operatorname{range}(N)\). Any two normal-equation solutions satisfy \(\Delta y_1-\Delta y_2\in\ker A^T\). Hence \(\Delta x=H^{-1}(q+A^T\Delta y)\) and \(\Delta s=r_d-A^T\Delta y\) are independent of the chosen multiplier solution. Full, augmented, and normal solutions correspond after quotienting multiplier directions by \(\ker A^T\). If \(g\notin\operatorname{range}(A)\), the systems are inconsistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With dependent constraint rows, compatible reductions recover invariant primal and slack directions while multipliers are ambiguous by the left null space; incompatible right-hand sides give no solution.
assumptions_latex: H\succ0
N=AH^{-1}A^T
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g\in\operatorname{range}(A)\Longrightarrow (\Delta x,\Delta s)\text{ are invariant over all normal-equation solutions}
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Solution-Set Correspondence

children.title: Dikin Local Geometry
children.top_down_role: Ellipsoidal local geometry induced by interior slack or variable scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Dikin Local Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-induced local norm and ellipsoid on the positive orthant within an affine slice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P^\circ=\{x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n:Ax=b\}\) and \(x\in P^\circ\), define the Dikin local norm on feasible displacements \(h\in\ker A\) by \[\|h\|_x=\|X^{-1}h\|_2=\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{h_i^2}{x_i^2}\right)^{1/2}.\] The radius-one Dikin ellipsoid is \(E_x=\{x+h:h\in\ker A,\ \|h\|_x<1\}\). Since \(|h_i|<x_i\) for every coordinate whenever \(\|h\|_x<1\), one has \(E_x\subseteq P^\circ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Dikin norm scales each feasible displacement by the current coordinates, and its open unit ellipsoid remains strictly feasible.
assumptions_latex: P^\circ\neq\varnothing
x\in P^\circ
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_x\subseteq P^\circ

notation.meaning: Open radius-one Dikin ellipsoid centered at x.

source_refs.locator: A Strictly Interior Point p. 29

source_witnesses.locator: A Strictly Interior Point p. 29

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness of radius one for positivity containment using only the diagonal local norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), \(\|h\|_x<1\) implies \(x+h>0\). The constant \(1\) is the largest universal radius with this property: for every \(r>1\), choose \(1<r'<r\) and set \(h=-r'x_je_j\); then \(\|h\|_x=r'<r\), but \(x_j+h_j=(1-r')x_j<0\). On an affine slice, this witness applies whenever its feasible-displacement space contains \(e_j\); without additional slice structure no larger universal radius is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The open unit Dikin ball is always interior, and no larger radius universally guarantees positivity without additional affine-slice structure.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|h\|_x<1\Rightarrow x+h>0,\qquad\text{and no universal }r>1\text{ has this implication}

notation.meaning: scalar strictly between one and the proposed radius

knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Universal Dikin Radius

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dikin Ellipsoid at a Positive Primal-Dual Pair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local scaled geometry for candidate next iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For componentwise positive vectors $x,s\in\mathbb{R}^n$, the Dikin ellipsoid at $(x,s)$ is
\[
\mathcal E_D(x,s):=\left\{(x+\Delta x,s+\Delta s)\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}:\left\|\frac{\Delta x}{x}+\frac{\Delta s}{s}\right\|\le 1\right\},
\]
where division is componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a positive primal-dual pair, the Dikin ellipsoid contains candidate next iterates whose summed componentwise relative primal and dual changes have norm at most one.
assumptions_latex: x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n
(\Delta x,\Delta s)\in\mathbb{R}^{2n}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x+\Delta x,s+\Delta s)\in\mathcal E_D(x,s)\iff\left\|\Delta x/x+\Delta s/s\right\|\le1

children.title: Diagonal-Scaling Metrics
children.top_down_role: Local metrics generated through diagonal primal or dual scalings.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Scaling Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate metric induced by diagonal rescaling at a positive primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), the primal diagonal-scaling metric is the positive-definite matrix \(G_x=X^{-2}=\operatorname{Diag}(x_1^{-2},\ldots,x_n^{-2})\). It defines the local inner product and norm \[\langle u,v\rangle_x=u^TG_xv,\qquad \|u\|_x=(u^TG_xu)^{1/2}=\|X^{-1}u\|_2.\] Its dual metric is \(G_x^{-1}=X^2\), so a covector \(g\) has dual norm \(\|g\|_{x,*}=(g^TX^2g)^{1/2}\). Both metrics are well defined precisely while every component of \(x\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The diagonal metric weights primal displacements by inverse coordinate size, while its dual weights covectors by coordinate size.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_x=X^{-2}\succ0,\qquad G_x^{-1}=X^2

notation.meaning: Norm induced by the inverse metric.

children.title: Primal-Dual Scaling Metrics
children.top_down_role: Coupled metrics balancing primal variables against dual slacks.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Scaling Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Paired diagonal metrics balancing positive primal and dual slack variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), define \(D=X^{1/2}S^{-1/2}=\operatorname{Diag}(\sqrt{x_i/s_i})\). The associated primal and dual local metrics are \[G_{x,s}=D^{-2}=X^{-1}S,\qquad G_{x,s}^{-1}=D^2=XS^{-1}.\] Accordingly, primal displacements and dual-slack displacements have norms \(\|u\|_{x,s}=\|D^{-1}u\|_2\) and \(\|v\|_{x,s,*}=\|Dv\|_2\). These norms are dual under the Euclidean pairing, and the Newton complementarity block uses the same primal metric \(X^{-1}S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive primal and slack vectors define reciprocal diagonal metrics that balance primal and dual-slack displacements componentwise.
assumptions_latex: x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n

notation.meaning: Primal metric induced by the primal-dual scaling.

children.title: Affine-Invariant Local Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Full-Space Local-Norm Transport Under Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hypotheses required for an affine pullback to define an isometry of genuine Hessian norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succeq0\) and consider the pullback quadratic form \(T^{\mathsf T}HT\). If \(T\) is singular, every nonzero \(k\in\ker T\) satisfies \(k^{\mathsf T}T^{\mathsf T}HTk=0\). If \(T\) is invertible but \(H\) has a nonzero null vector \(v\), then \(k=T^{-1}v\ne0\) has the same property. Thus a singular coordinate map or a non-positive-definite Hessian yields only a seminorm on the full coordinate space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular coordinate map or a positive-semidefinite Hessian with a null direction makes the transported quadratic form degenerate.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is symmetric positive semidefinite.
The pullback quadratic form is \(T^{\mathsf T}HT\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ singular, or }(T\text{ invertible and }H\not\succ0),\quad\Longrightarrow\quad T^{\mathsf T}HT\not\succ0.

notation.meaning: barrier Hessian at the represented point
linear part of the affine coordinate map

knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Full-Space Local-Norm Transport Under Degeneracy

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Covariance of the Dual Local Norm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cotangent-space counterpart of affine transport for a positive-definite barrier Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H=\nabla^2F(x)\succ0, let x=Tz+d with T nonsingular, and set \widetilde H=T^{\mathsf T}HT. For a covector g in x-coordinates, its z-coordinate representation is \widetilde g=T^{\mathsf T}g. Then \[\|\widetilde g\|_{z,*}^2=\widetilde g^{\mathsf T}\widetilde H^{-1}\widetilde g=g^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}g=\|g\|_{x,*}^2.\] Thus affine pullback is an isometry for dual covector norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an invertible affine coordinate change, covectors transform by the transpose map and their inverse-Hessian local norm is unchanged.
assumptions_latex: H=\nabla^2F(x)\succ0.
T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\text{ is nonsingular}.
\widetilde H=T^{\mathsf T}HT\text{ and }\widetilde g=T^{\mathsf T}g.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affine Invariance of Self-Concordant Barrier Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine pullback preserves the differential inequalities governing intrinsic self-concordant barrier geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on an open convex set \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(x=Tz+d\) with \(T\) nonsingular, and define \(\widetilde Q=\{z:Tz+d\in Q\}\) and \(\widetilde F(z)=F(Tz+d)\). Then \(\widetilde F\) is a \(
u\)-self-concordant barrier on \(\widetilde Q\). For every direction \(h\), \[D^k\widetilde F(z)[h,\ldots,h]=D^kF(x)[Th,\ldots,Th]\quad(k=1,2,3),\] so the self-concordance and barrier-gradient inequalities retain the same parameter \(
u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine reparameterization preserves self-concordance and the barrier parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a \(\nu\)-self-concordant barrier on \(Q\).
\(T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular.
\(\widetilde F=F\circ(z\mapsto Tz+d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde F\text{ is a }\nu\text{-self-concordant barrier on }\widetilde Q.

notation.meaning: kth derivative multilinear form of the barrier

Affine-Invariant Local Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covariance of logarithmic-barrier local norms under invertible affine coordinate changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be a twice differentiable barrier on an open convex domain \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(
abla^2F(x)\succ0\). For an invertible affine change \(x=Tz+d\), define \(\widetilde F(z)=F(Tz+d)\). Then \[
abla^2\widetilde F(z)=T^T
abla^2F(x)T\] and, for every displacement \(k\), \[\|k\|_{z,\widetilde F}^2=k^T
abla^2\widetilde F(z)k=(Tk)^T
abla^2F(x)(Tk)=\|Tk\|_{x,F}^2.\] Hence affine coordinate changes transport local balls and lengths without changing their intrinsic barrier geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine coordinate change transports the barrier Hessian by congruence and preserves corresponding local lengths and balls.
assumptions_latex: T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\text{ is invertible}
F\in C^2(Q),\ \nabla^2F(x)\succ0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|k\|_{z,\widetilde F}=\|Tk\|_{x,F}

children.title: Metric Degeneration Near Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Loss of balanced local geometry as iterates approach faces or degenerate solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Condition-Number Growth Requires Relative Coordinate Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes divergence of absolute metric scale from anisotropic degeneration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) and \(G_x=X^{-2}\), \[\kappa_2(G_x)=\left(\frac{\max_i x_i}{\min_i x_i}\right)^2.\] Hence \(\min_i x_i^k\to0\) forces \(\kappa_2(G_{x^k})\to\infty\) when \(\max_i x_i^k\) stays bounded below by a positive constant. A vanishing coordinate alone is insufficient: if \(x^k=t_ke\) with \(t_k\downarrow0\), then \(G_{x^k}=t_k^{-2}I\) and \(\kappa_2(G_{x^k})=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The metric becomes ill-conditioned only when coordinates separate relatively; uniform approach to the boundary can preserve its condition number despite divergent scale.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
Condition number is measured in the Euclidean spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa_2(G_{x^k})=\left(\frac{\max_i x_i^k}{\min_i x_i^k}\right)^2;\text{ divergence occurs exactly when this coordinate ratio diverges.}
knowledge_statements.title: Condition-Number Growth Requires Relative Coordinate Separation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Volumetric manifestation of boundary degeneration for the positive-orthant logarithmic metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n, let G_x=X^{-2} and E_x=\{h:h^{\mathsf T}G_xh\le1\}. Then E_x=XB_2^n and \[\operatorname{vol}(E_x)=\operatorname{vol}(B_2^n)\det X=\operatorname{vol}(B_2^n)\prod_{i=1}^n x_i.\] Consequently, if x^k remains bounded and \min_i x_i^k\to0, then \operatorname{vol}(E_{x^k})\to0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full-space Dikin ellipsoid has volume proportional to the product of the positive coordinates, so its Euclidean volume collapses during a bounded approach to the boundary.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n.
For the limiting assertion, (x^k) is bounded and \min_i x_i^k\to0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{vol}(E_x)=\operatorname{vol}(B_2^n)\prod_i x_i,\qquad \operatorname{vol}(E_{x^k})\to0.

notation.meaning: unit ellipsoid of the inverse-square diagonal metric
Euclidean unit ball in dimension n

knowledge_statements.title: Collapse of Full-Space Dikin-Ellipsoid Volume

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infinite Local-Metric Distance to an Orthant Face
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic-distance manifestation of boundary degeneration for the inverse-square diagonal metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equip \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\) with the Riemannian metric \(G_x=X^{-2}\). The coordinatewise logarithm map is an isometry onto Euclidean space, and therefore \[d_G(x,y)=\|\log y-\log x\|_2.\] For fixed \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), if \(y_j^k\to0\) for some coordinate \(j\), then \(d_G(x,y^k)\to\infty\). Thus every orthant boundary face is at infinite intrinsic distance despite being at finite Euclidean distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logarithmic coordinates flatten the inverse-square metric, so approaching a zero coordinate requires infinite intrinsic distance.
assumptions_latex: x,y^k\in\mathbb R_{++}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_G(x,y)=\|\log y-\log x\|_2,\qquad y_j^k\to0\Longrightarrow d_G(x,y^k)\to\infty
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Local-Metric Distance to an Orthant Face
Metric Degeneration Near Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniform conditioning as positive coordinates approach the orthant boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^k\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) converge to a boundary point \(\bar x\geq0\), and suppose \(x_j^k\to0\) for some coordinate \(j\). For the diagonal metric \(G_{x^k}=(X^k)^{-2}\), \[e_j^TG_{x^k}e_j=(x_j^k)^{-2}\to\infty,\qquad e_j^TG_{x^k}^{-1}e_j=(x_j^k)^2\to0.\] Thus the primal metric becomes unbounded and its inverse becomes singular in the boundary coordinate. Consequently, no Euclidean-uniform upper and lower spectral bounds for this local metric can persist along such a sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As a positive coordinate approaches zero, its primal metric weight diverges and the corresponding inverse-metric weight vanishes, destroying uniform conditioning.
assumptions_latex: x^k\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n
x_j^k\to0\text{ for some }j
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda_{\max}(G_{x^k})\to\infty,\qquad \lambda_{\min}(G_{x^k}^{-1})\to0

children.title: Interiority Step-Control Family

children.title: Fraction-to-Boundary Control
children.top_down_role: Step restrictions designed to retain strict positivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Fraction-to-Boundary Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step-length rule retaining a prescribed fraction of current positivity margins.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), a direction \((\Delta x,\Delta s)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\tau\in(0,1)\), compute the uncapped boundary-contact steps \[\alpha_x^{\max}=\min_{\Delta x_i<0}\frac{-x_i}{\Delta x_i},\qquad \alpha_s^{\max}=\min_{\Delta s_i<0}\frac{-s_i}{\Delta s_i},\] where an empty minimum equals \(+\infty\). Set \[\alpha=\min\{1,\tau\alpha_x^{\max},\tau\alpha_s^{\max}\}\] and output \((x^+,s^+)=(x+\alpha\Delta x,s+\alpha\Delta s)\). Then \(x^+,s^+\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\); moreover, every decreasing component satisfies \(x_i^+\geq(1-\tau)x_i\) or \(s_i^+\geq(1-\tau)s_i\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The step is limited to one and to a fixed fraction of each first boundary-contact step, thereby guaranteeing strict positivity while permitting a full step when it is sufficiently short.
assumptions_latex: x,s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n
\tau\in(0,1)
\Delta x,\Delta s\in\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x+\alpha\Delta x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n,\qquad s+\alpha\Delta s\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n

notation.meaning: Uncapped steps to the first primal and slack boundary contacts, with value +infinity when no component decreases.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Strict-Positivity Boundary for the Fraction Parameter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint boundary for a nontrivial fraction-to-boundary rule with a uniform positive margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\alpha=\min\{1,\tau\alpha_x^{\max},\tau\alpha_s^{\max}\}\), every \(\tau\in(0,1)\) leaves \(x_i^+\ge(1-\tau)x_i>0\) and \(s_i^+\ge(1-\tau)s_i>0\) on decreasing components. At \(\tau=1\), strict positivity is no longer guaranteed: if \(x_1=1\), \(\Delta x_1=-1\), and no smaller limit is active, then \(\alpha=1\) and \(x_1^+=0\). At \(\tau=0\) the rule makes no progress, and negative \(\tau\) is not a forward fraction-to-boundary step. Thus \(0<\tau<1\) is the sharp range for positive progress with a uniform strict-interiority margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fraction strictly between zero and one is necessary for positive progress with a guaranteed boundary margin; at one the step may hit the boundary exactly.

knowledge_statements.title: Centrality-Restoration Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrector control for returning a feasible primal-dual iterate toward the central path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(x>0\), \(s>0\), let \(X=\operatorname{Diag}(x)\), \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), and \(\mu=x^{\mathsf T}s/n\). \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), and \(x,s>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Merit-Based Step Acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo acceptance for a positivity-constrained primal-dual merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi\) be continuously differentiable on the strictly positive primal-dual domain, let \(z=(x,y,s)\), and let \(d\) satisfy \(\nabla\Phi(z)^{\mathsf T}d<0\). For fixed \(\gamma\in(0,1)\) and \(\rho\in(0,1)\), accept the first trial step \(\alpha=\rho^j\), \(j\in\{0,1,\ldots\}\), for which \(x+\alpha d_x>0\), \(s+\alpha d_s>0\), and \(\Phi(z+\alpha d)\leq\Phi(z)+\gamma\alpha\nabla\Phi(z)^{\mathsf T}d\). If no such trial is yet found, increment \(j\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For interior iterates \(z^k=(x^k,y^k,s^k)\) and directions \(d^k=(d_x^k,d_y^k,d_s^k)\), define \(\alpha_{\max}^k=\min\{1,\min_{i:d_{x,i}^k<0}(-x_i^k/d_{x,i}^k),\min_{i:d_{s,i}^k<0}(-s_i^k/d_{s,i}^k)\}\), with \(\min\varnothing=+\infty\). A boundary-stalling regime occurs when \(\alpha_{\max}^k\to0\) while a selected optimality residual \(R_k\) satisfies \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}R_k>0\). One sufficient step-limiting mechanism is the existence of indices \(i_k\) and \(\delta>0\) such that \(x_{i_k}^k\downarrow0\) and \(d_{x,i_k}^k\leq-\delta\), because then \(\alpha_{\max}^k\leq x_{i_k}^k/\delta\to0\); the analogous statement holds for \(s^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundary stalling means that positivity-preserving steps tend to zero while a specified optimality residual stays bounded away from zero. A shrinking primal or dual component with a uniformly negative direction component is one mechanism that forces this behavior.
