knowledge_statements.statement_title: Low-Rank Form of a Partial Normal-Matrix Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic representation induced by refreshing a selected subset of diagonal scaling entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=AD^2A^{\mathsf T}\), and change \(d_i^2\) by \(\delta_i\) only for \(i\in I\). If \(a_i\) is column \(i\) of \(A\), then
\[
\widehat M-M=\sum_{i\in I}\delta_i a_i a_i^{\mathsf T}=A_I\operatorname{Diag}(\delta_I)A_I^{\mathsf T},
\qquad \operatorname{rank}(\widehat M-M)\le |I|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refreshing selected diagonal scalings changes the normal matrix by at most one rank-one contribution per refreshed index.
assumptions_latex: Only squared scaling entries indexed by \(I\) change.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat M-M=A_I\operatorname{Diag}(\delta_I)A_I^{\mathsf T},\qquad \operatorname{rank}(\widehat M-M)\le |I|.

notation.meaning: columns of A indexed by the refresh set
change in squared scaling entry i

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Form of a Partial Normal-Matrix Refresh
Partial Local-System Updating
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate normal-equation solves obtained by refreshing only selected entries of the local diagonal scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(A\), a positive scaling \(D_0\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and an initial factorization of \(M_0=AD_0^2A^{\mathsf T}\), iteration \(k\) selects an index set \(I_k\). Define
\[
(\widetilde D_k)_{ii}=\begin{cases}(D_k)_{ii},&i\in I_k,\\(\widetilde D_{k-1})_{ii},&i\notin I_k,\end{cases}
\qquad \widetilde M_k=A\widetilde D_k^2A^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Update only the contributions indexed by \(I_k\), solve \(\widetilde M_k\Delta y=r_k\), and recover the remaining Newton components. Accept only if the true Newton residual meets the forcing test; otherwise enlarge \(I_k\) or refactorize. Stop at the prescribed primal-dual residual and complementarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refresh selected scaling contributions, reuse the remaining local system, and accept the approximate Newton direction only when its true residual passes a forcing test.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank and every retained diagonal scaling is positive.
The acceptance test evaluates the residual of the current, not stale, Newton system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted direction satisfies the prescribed inexact-Newton residual test; failed tests trigger additional updates or refactorization.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No evidence is supplied for the selective refresh policy, forcing test, or fallback regime. A dedicated source is required before this algorithm can enter candidate-review knowledge.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accumulated Change Between Consecutive Component Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-specific lower bound between consecutive updates of one stored component; the parameter \(\sigma\) retains its surrounding algorithmic meaning because the extract supplies no separate domain assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that component \(\widetilde{s}_i\) is updated at iteration \(k_1\) and next updated at iteration \(k_2>k_1\). If \(\Delta s_i^{k+1}\) denotes the \(i\)-th coordinate of the modified Newton step at iteration \(k+1\), then \[\sum_{k=k_1}^{k_2-1}\left|\frac{\Delta s_i^{k+1}}{s_i^k}\right|\geq 1-\frac{1}{\sigma}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a stored component is updated at iteration k1 and next updated at k2, then the accumulated absolute modified-Newton change normalized by the current component is at least one minus the reciprocal of the algorithmic parameter sigma.
assumptions_latex: \widetilde{s}_i\text{ is updated at }k_1\text{ and next updated at }k_2
\Delta s_i^{k+1}\text{ denotes the }i\text{-th coordinate of the modified Newton step at iteration }k+1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{k=k_1}^{k_2-1}\left|\frac{\Delta s_i^{k+1}}{s_i^k}\right|\geq 1-\frac{1}{\sigma}

children.title: Rank-One Factor Updating
children.top_down_role: Structured rank-one modifications of local-system factors or approximations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic comparison after one scaling contribution changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M\in\mathbb S_{++}^m\) with a stored dense Cholesky factor, a rank-one Cholesky update, or an admissible downdate whose result remains positive definite, uses \(O(m^2)\) arithmetic and retains \(O(m^2)\) factor storage. Recomputing a dense Cholesky factor from scratch uses \(O(m^3)\) arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense rank-one Cholesky modification is quadratic in the system order, compared with cubic refactorization work.
assumptions_latex: A dense Cholesky factor of the reference SPD matrix is available.
For a downdate, the updated matrix remains positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{rank1}}(m)=O(m^2),\qquad T_{\mathrm{refactor}}(m)=O(m^3).
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Rank-One Cholesky Update Work
Rank-One Factor Updating
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one modification of a normal-equation matrix when one diagonal scaling entry changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=AD^2A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), and suppose only \(d_j^2\) changes to \(\widehat d_j^2\). With \(a_j\) the \(j\)-th column of \(A\) and \(\delta=\widehat d_j^2-d_j^2\),
\[
\widehat M=M+\delta a_ja_j^{\mathsf T}.
\]
If \(1+\delta a_j^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}a_j>0\), then \(\widehat M\succ0\) and
\[
\widehat M^{-1}=M^{-1}-\frac{\delta M^{-1}a_ja_j^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}}{1+\delta a_j^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}a_j}.
\]
Equivalently, a Cholesky factor of \(M\) can be rank-one updated when \(\delta>0\) or safely downdated when the displayed positivity condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing one scaling entry changes the normal matrix by rank one, permitting an inverse or Cholesky update when positive definiteness is preserved.
assumptions_latex: \(M=AD^2A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
Exactly one squared scaling entry changes.
\(1+\delta a_j^{\mathsf T}M^{-1}a_j>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat M=M+\delta a_ja_j^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and its inverse is given by the displayed rank-one formula.

notation.meaning: change in the squared scaling entry

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-one identity and Sherman–Morrison formula are standard and algebraically appropriate, but the record has no evidence. The terminal method container may also be better served by an algorithm or property record than by a representation.

children.title: Selective Scaling Updates
children.top_down_role: Partial renewal of scaling or metric information between iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Selective Scaling Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold-based refreshing of diagonal scaling entries with a spectral-accuracy safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given current positive scaling \(D_k\), stored scaling \(\widetilde D_{k-1}\), threshold \(\tau>0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\), select
\[
I_k=\{i:|\log (D_k)_{ii}-\log(\widetilde D_{k-1})_{ii}|>\tau\}.
\]
Set \((\widetilde D_k)_{ii}=(D_k)_{ii}\) on \(I_k\) and retain the stored value otherwise. Form or update \(\widetilde M_k=A\widetilde D_k^2A^{\mathsf T}\), solve the approximate Newton system, and accept only after a true-residual test. Moreover, if \(|(\widetilde D_k)_{ii}^2/(D_k)_{ii}^2-1|\le\eta<1\) for all \(i\), then
\[
(1-\eta)M_k\preceq\widetilde M_k\preceq(1+\eta)M_k.
\]
Stop at the requested primal-dual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update scaling entries whose logarithms moved beyond a threshold; bounded entrywise staleness yields a corresponding spectral approximation of the normal matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(D_k\) and \(\widetilde D_k\) are positive diagonal matrices.
\(A\) has full row rank.
For the spectral bound, every squared scaling ratio differs from one by at most \(\eta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selective update is accepted only after residual verification, and its normal matrix satisfies \((1-\eta)M_k\preceq\widetilde M_k\preceq(1+\eta)M_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional spectral inequality is mathematically sound, but no source supports the logarithmic threshold rule, residual-verification policy, or reuse algorithm. A dedicated locator is required.

children.title: Update-Reuse Regimes
children.top_down_role: Conditions supporting reuse of prior local-system information.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Spectral Equivalence Does Not Make a Stale Direct Solve Exact
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating approximate or preconditioned reuse from exact reuse of unchanged factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) and \(\widehat H\) be SPD and let \(d=H^{-1}b\). If the factors of \(H\) are applied without modification to the changed system \(\widehat H d=b\), then the current-system residual is
\[
r=b-\widehat H d=(H-\widehat H)H^{-1}b.
\]
Thus spectral equivalence can control approximation quality but does not make the stale direct solve exact. Exactness for the particular right-hand side requires \((H-\widehat H)H^{-1}b=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectrally close old factor is an approximate solver or preconditioner, not an exact factorization of the changed matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(H,\widehat H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
The old factors are applied without updating them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r=b-\widehat H H^{-1}b=(H-\widehat H)H^{-1}b.

notation.meaning: residual in the current linear system

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Equivalence Does Not Make a Stale Direct Solve Exact

assumptions_latex: For each iteration \(t\), \(H_t\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^n\) is the symmetric positive-definite local-system matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The factorization or preconditioner built from \(H_t\) is spectrally reusable throughout the largest interval satisfying the displayed inequalities.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard SPD spectral-equivalence criterion for preconditioner reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral regime for reusing an SPD local-system factorization or preconditioner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\eta\ge 0\). A factorization or preconditioner formed from \(H_t\) is in an \(\eta\)-update-reuse regime through iteration \(t+r\) when, for every \(0\le j\le r\), \[e^{-\eta}H_t\preceq H_{t+j}\preceq e^{\eta}H_t.\] Equivalently, every eigenvalue of \(H_t^{-1/2}H_{t+j}H_t^{-1/2}\) lies in \([e^{-\eta},e^{\eta}]\), and hence \[\kappa_2\!\left(H_t^{-1/2}H_{t+j}H_t^{-1/2}\right)\le e^{2\eta}.\] Rebuilding is required once the prescribed spectral-drift tolerance is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local-system factorization remains reusable while every updated matrix stays spectrally equivalent to the reference matrix within the chosen multiplicative tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Update-Reuse Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The spectral-equivalence condition is mathematically coherent and fits the Update-Reuse Regimes container, but no inspectable citation supports its interpretation as a reuse or rebuilding criterion for the intended interior-point local systems.

children.title: Update-Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where accumulated approximation error or changing geometry makes structured reuse unreliable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient stability control for a sequence of symmetric updates relative to one SPD reference matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_0\succ0\) and \(H_k=H_0+\sum_{j=1}^kE_j\), where every \(E_j\) is symmetric. Define
\[
\rho_j=\|H_0^{-1/2}E_jH_0^{-1/2}\|_2,\qquad R_k=\sum_{j=1}^k\rho_j.
\]
If \(R_k<1\), then
\[
(1-R_k)H_0\preceq H_k\preceq(1+R_k)H_0,
\qquad
\|H_0^{1/2}(H_k^{-1}-H_0^{-1})H_0^{1/2}\|_2\le\frac{R_k}{1-R_k}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative errors from successive structured updates accumulate; a total bound below one preserves positive definiteness and controls inverse drift.
assumptions_latex: \(H_0\) is SPD.

assumptions_latex: The standard-form primal-dual pair is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^n\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(z=(x,y,s)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(D\ge1\). For each coordinate \(z_i\), reconstruct the unique reduced fraction \(p_i/q_i\) satisfying \(1\le q_i\le D\) and \(|z_i-p_i/q_i|<1/(2D^2)\); report failure if no such unique fraction exists. Assemble \(\widehat z=(\widehat x,\widehat y,\widehat s)\) and verify exactly that \[A\widehat x=b,\quad A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y+\widehat s=c,\quad \widehat x\ge0,\quad \widehat s\ge0,\quad \widehat x^{\mathsf T}\widehat s=0.\] Output \(\widehat z\) only if every check passes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruct bounded-denominator rational coordinates from a sufficiently accurate iterate, then output them only after exact primal feasibility, dual feasibility, nonnegativity, and complementarity checks pass.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\ge1\), let \(z_i^*\in\mathbb{Q}\) have reduced denominator at most \(D\), and let \(z_i\in\mathbb{R}\) satisfy \(|z_i-z_i^*|<1/(2D^2)\). Then \(z_i^*\) is the unique rational with reduced denominator at most \(D\) in the interval \((z_i-1/(2D^2),z_i+1/(2D^2))\). Coordinatewise reconstruction under this condition must be followed by exact primal-dual verification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp uniform uniqueness radius for reduced rationals with bounded denominators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\ge2\). Any distinct reduced rationals \(p/q\) and \(r/s\), with positive denominators \(q,s\le D\), satisfy \[\left|\frac pq-\frac rs\right|\ge\frac1{D(D-1)}.\] Consequently, if \(z^*\) has reduced denominator at most \(D\) and \(|z-z^*|<1/(2D(D-1))\), then \(z^*\) is the unique admissible rational in that open ball. The spacing is attained by \(1/D\) and \(1/(D-1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact minimum spacing between distinct rationals with denominators at most D is 1/(D(D-1)), yielding the sharp open half-spacing uniqueness radius.
assumptions_latex: \(D\ge2\) is an integer.
Candidates are reduced rationals with positive denominator at most \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sharp uniform open-ball uniqueness radius is \(1/(2D(D-1))\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Finite-D Denominator Spacing Regime

children.title: Recovery Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Degeneracy, ambiguity, or insufficient accuracy obstructing exact recovery.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-D midpoint counterexample for coordinatewise bounded-denominator reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every integer \(D\ge2\), let \(a=1/D\), \(b=1/(D-1)\), and \(z=(a+b)/2\). Both \(a\) and \(b\) are reduced rationals with denominators at most \(D\), and \[|a-b|=\frac1{D(D-1)},\qquad |z-a|=|z-b|=\frac1{2D(D-1)}.\] Hence proximity alone cannot uniquely select an admissible rational at this half-spacing radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The midpoint of 1/D and 1/(D-1) is equally close to two admissible bounded-denominator rationals.
assumptions_latex: \(D\ge2\) is an integer.
Recovery uses only proximity and the reduced-denominator bound \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform uniqueness fails at error radius \(1/(2D(D-1))\).
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Bounded-Denominator Ambiguity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure modes of the auxiliary positivity-margin recovery method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proposed partition \((B,N)\), consider the auxiliary constraints \(Ax=b\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y+s=c\), \(x_N=0\), \(s_B=0\), \(x_B\ge\tau\mathbf1\), \(s_N\ge\tau\mathbf1\), and \(\tau\ge0\). If this system is infeasible, or if every feasible point has \(\tau=0\), then the partition is not realized by any strictly complementary primal-dual optimum and must be rejected. An unbounded positive margin is not a failure: feasibility with any \(\tau>0\) already supplies the required strict signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proposed partition fails strictly complementary recovery exactly when the auxiliary system has no feasible positive-margin point.
assumptions_latex: \((B,N)\) is a proposed partition of the variable indices.
The auxiliary constraints are tested exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The partition is recoverable strictly complementarily iff the auxiliary system admits a feasible point with \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Complementarity Recovery Rejection Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure when the asserted reconstruction bound excludes the exact target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*=p/q\) be reduced and suppose reconstruction searches only rationals with denominator at most \(D<q\). Even with exact input \(z=z^*\), the target lies outside the candidate set, so bounded-denominator reconstruction cannot be guaranteed to return \(z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An underestimated denominator bound can prevent recovery even when the approximation is exact.
assumptions_latex: \(z^*=p/q\) is reduced.
The reconstruction bound satisfies \(D<q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact recovery of \(z^*\) is not guaranteed even at zero approximation error.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Denominator-Bound Boundary

assumptions_latex: Recovery uses only coordinatewise proximity and a denominator bound \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At error radius \(1/(2D^2)\) or larger, bounded-denominator rational recovery is not uniformly unique; absent exact verification, rounding can return a false solution.

children.title: Optimal-Basis Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of a basic optimal representation for simplex-oriented postprocessing.

assumptions_latex: The standard-form LP is \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^n\).
A candidate set \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) satisfies \(|B|=m\), and \(A_B\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The candidate \(B\) is an optimal basis exactly when its associated vectors satisfy \(x_B\ge0\) and \(s_N\ge0\).

If either inequality fails, this candidate basis is rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the basic primal variables and nonbasic reduced costs exactly; their nonnegativity certifies the candidate as an optimal basis, while failure of either sign test rejects it.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Enumerate every \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(|B|=m\). Discard \(B\) if \(A_B\) is singular. For each remaining candidate, compute exactly \[x_B=A_B^{-1}b,\quad x_N=0,\quad y=A_B^{-\mathsf T}c_B,\quad s_B=0,\quad s_N=c_N-A_N^{\mathsf T}y.\] Return the first candidate satisfying \(x_B\ge0\) and \(s_N\ge0\). If none passes, report that no optimal basis exists. Whenever the LP has an optimal basic feasible solution, the enumeration returns an optimal basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumerate nonsingular column subsets and apply exact primal-feasibility and reduced-cost tests until an optimal basis is found.

All linear algebra and sign tests are exact.
The LP has an optimal basic feasible solution for the success guarantee.

The procedure is finite, but its candidate count can be exponential and therefore gives no polynomial-time guarantee.

assumptions_latex: Candidate bases are all \(m\)-subsets of the \(n\) columns.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta>0\) denote the minimum separation relevant to the recovery task, such as the smallest positive complementary component, the distance to an incorrect partition, or the spacing between admissible bounded-denominator rationals. If a certified bound \(E_k\) satisfies \(E_k<\Delta/2\), then nearest-object or threshold recovery is unique and can be checked exactly. Thus finite termination occurs at \[K=\min\{k:E_k<\Delta/2\},\] provided this set is nonempty. Convergence without a known positive separation does not itself supply a certified finite stopping index.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact recovery becomes certifiable once the error falls below half a positive data-dependent separation; convergence alone does not identify when that happens.

children.title: Normal-Equation Factorization
children.top_down_role: Sparse positive-definite factorization and its conditioning tradeoffs.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(X,S\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) are positive diagonal matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H=AWA^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), \(PHP^{\mathsf T}=LL^{\mathsf T}\), and \(\kappa_2(H)=\kappa_2(AW^{1/2})^2\).

notation.meaning: scaled rectangular matrix whose Gram matrix is \(H\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-complement realization of an LP primal-dual Newton system and its conditioning tradeoff.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(X,S\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be positive diagonal matrices, set \(W=XS^{-1}\), and let \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(r_p\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Consider
\[-W^{-1}\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y=q,\qquad A\Delta x=r_p.\]
Eliminating \(\Delta x\) gives
\[H\Delta y=(AWA^{\mathsf T})\Delta y=r_p+AWq,\qquad \Delta x=W(A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y-q).\]
If \(A\) has full row rank, then \(H\succ0\) and, after a symmetric permutation \(P\), admits a Cholesky factorization \(PHP^{\mathsf T}=LL^{\mathsf T}\). With \(B=AW^{1/2}\), one has \(H=BB^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\kappa_2(H)=\kappa_2(B)^2\), so forming the normal equations squares the spectral condition number of the scaled rectangular matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal direction yields a positive-definite weighted normal equation when the constraint matrix has full row rank. Sparse Cholesky can then be used, but the normal matrix has the square of the scaled rectangular matrix's spectral condition number.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Equation Factorization

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact condition for ordinary positive-definite Cholesky factorization of the weighted normal matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\succ0\) and \(H=AWA^T\). Then \[v^THv=\|W^{1/2}A^Tv\|_2^2,\qquad \operatorname{rank}(H)=\operatorname{rank}(A).\] Consequently, ordinary Cholesky factorization with strictly positive pivots exists exactly when \(A\) has full row rank. If \(A\) is row-rank deficient, \(H\) is positive semidefinite and singular, requiring dependency removal, a rank-revealing semidefinite factorization, or regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The weighted normal matrix supports ordinary positive-definite Cholesky exactly for independent constraint rows.
assumptions_latex: W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n},\ W\succ0
A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AWA^T\succ0\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{rank}(A)=m
knowledge_statements.title: Cholesky Rank Boundary

children.title: Augmented-System Factorization
children.top_down_role: Symmetric indefinite and quasidefinite realization of coupled systems.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is positive diagonal.
\(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(r_p\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(\rho,delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unregularized \(K\) is symmetric and is nonsingular indefinite when \(m\geq1\) and \(A\) has full row rank; \(K_{\rho,delta}\) is symmetric quasidefinite and nonsingular for every \(A\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric coupled realization before normal-equation elimination, including its quasidefinite regularization.

source_refs.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), let \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be positive diagonal, and let \(q\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(r_p\in\mathbb{R}^m\). The reduced Newton equations have the coupled representation
\[K\begin{pmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}q\\r_p\end{pmatrix},\qquad K=\begin{pmatrix}-D^{-2}&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}.\]
The matrix \(K\) is symmetric. If \(m\geq1\) and \(A\) has full row rank, then \(K\) is nonsingular and indefinite and may be solved by a symmetric-indefinite factorization. For any \(A\) and any \(\rho,delta>0\), the regularized matrix
\[K_{\rho,delta}=\begin{pmatrix}-(D^{-2}+\rho I)&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&\delta I\end{pmatrix}\]
is symmetric quasidefinite, because its leading diagonal block is negative definite and its trailing diagonal block is positive definite, and it is nonsingular even when \(A\) is rank deficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coupled Newton matrix is symmetric and, under full row rank, nonsingular indefinite. Positive shifts on its primal and dual diagonal blocks produce a symmetric quasidefinite matrix that is nonsingular even for rank-deficient constraint matrices.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-System Factorization

source_witnesses.locator: Primal-Dual Methods: Development of the Fundamental Ideas p. 43

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct factorization interface for a nonsingular augmented Newton matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular symmetric augmented matrix \(K\), choose a symmetric permutation \(P\) and compute \[PKP^T=LDL^T,\] where \(L\) is unit lower triangular and \(D\) is block diagonal with nonsingular \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) pivot blocks. Solve \(Kz=r\) by permutation, triangular substitution, a block-diagonal solve, and reverse substitution. Symmetric pivoting is generally required because a nonsingular indefinite matrix may have a zero or unsafe prospective \(1\times1\) pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular augmented system is solved by a symmetrically pivoted block LDL-transpose factorization using one-by-one and two-by-two pivots.
assumptions_latex: K=K^T
K\text{ is nonsingular}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: PKP^T=LDL^T

notation.meaning: Triangular factor and block-diagonal pivot factor.

knowledge_statements.title: Pivoted Symmetric-Indefinite Solve

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation boundary for quasidefinite regularization of an augmented system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K_{\rho,\delta}=K+E_{\rho,\delta}\). If \(K_{\rho,\delta}z_{\rho,\delta}=r\), then its residual in the original equations is \[r-Kz_{\rho,\delta}=E_{\rho,\delta}z_{\rho,\delta}.\] Thus regularization guarantees nonsingularity of the modified system but does not produce an exact solution of the original equations unless this perturbation residual vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quasidefinite regularization makes the modified matrix nonsingular, but its solution generally solves perturbed rather than original Newton equations.
assumptions_latex: K_{\rho,\delta}=K+E_{\rho,\delta}
K_{\rho,\delta}z_{\rho,\delta}=r

children.title: Sparse Ordering Strategies
children.top_down_role: Ordering choices used to preserve sparse factorization structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case computational boundary for exact minimum-fill ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an undirected graph \(G\) and an integer \(K\), deciding whether some elimination ordering introduces at most \(K\) fill edges is NP-complete. Therefore computing a globally minimum-fill ordering is NP-hard, and minimum-degree, approximate-minimum-degree, nested-dissection, and related strategies generally provide fill-reducing heuristics rather than global minimum-fill guarantees unless additional graph structure is assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Globally minimizing elimination fill is NP-hard, so practical sparse orderings generally optimize fill or work proxies heuristically.
assumptions_latex: Fill is measured by graph edges added during symmetric elimination.
The graph \(G\) and threshold \(K\) are explicitly represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(G,K):G\text{ has an elimination ordering adding at most }K\text{ edges}\}\text{ is NP-complete}.

notation.meaning: allowed number of added fill edges

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Fill Ordering Hardness
Sparse Ordering Strategies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic permutation selection for sparse symmetric factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a sparse symmetric matrix \(H\), construct its undirected sparsity graph \(G(H)\). Choose a permutation \(P\) by a fill-reducing heuristic, such as approximate minimum degree, or by nested dissection using graph separators. Perform symbolic elimination on \(PHP^{\mathsf T}\) to determine the elimination tree and predicted factor pattern. If the predicted storage or frontal sizes exceed prescribed limits, revise the ordering; otherwise numerically factor \(PHP^{\mathsf T}\). The output is \(P\) together with the symbolic factor structure. The heuristic minimizes a fill or work proxy and need not attain the globally minimum-fill ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A graph heuristic permutes a sparse Newton matrix before symbolic and numerical factorization to reduce predicted fill, memory, or frontal work.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}\) is sparse and symmetric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a symmetric permutation \(P\) and a predicted factor pattern for \(PHP^{\mathsf T}\).

notation.meaning: undirected sparsity graph of the symmetric matrix

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the Sparse Ordering Strategies leaf, and the distinction between heuristic fill reduction and globally minimum fill is appropriate. No source is supplied for approximate minimum degree, nested dissection, symbolic elimination, or the elimination-tree output.

children.title: Fill-In Control
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms limiting factor growth during sparse elimination.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact graph condition for symmetric elimination without structural fill.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be the structural graph of a symmetric matrix and let \(\pi\) be a fixed elimination ordering. Elimination in order \(\pi\) introduces no fill if and only if, for every vertex \(v\), the neighbors of \(v\) occurring later than \(v\) in \(\pi\) form a clique. Such a \(\pi\) is a perfect elimination ordering. Consequently, \(G\) admits a zero-fill ordering if and only if \(G\) is chordal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ordering is fill-free exactly when every vertex's later neighbors form a clique; a fill-free ordering exists exactly for chordal graphs.
assumptions_latex: A fixed symmetric elimination ordering is used.
Structural dropping and numerical pivot reordering are absent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pi\text{ introduces no fill}\iff\pi\text{ is a perfect elimination ordering},\qquad \exists\pi\text{ with no fill}\iff G\text{ is chordal}.
knowledge_statements.title: Perfect-Elimination No-Fill Characterization
Fill-In Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph characterization and cost criterion for factor fill.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a symmetric permutation \(P\), eliminating \(PHP^{\mathsf T}\) adds an edge between every pair of currently adjacent, uneliminated neighbors of each pivot. The resulting filled graph determines the structural nonzeros of the triangular factor \(L\). Consequently, ordering, symbolic amalgamation, and pivot restrictions control storage and arithmetic through quantities such as \(\operatorname{nnz}(L)\) and \(\sum_j \operatorname{nnz}(L_{:,j})^2\). Numerical cancellation does not justify omitting a structurally predicted entry unless an explicit dropping rule is used, and unrestricted stability pivoting can introduce fill beyond the symbolic prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elimination creates clique edges among remaining pivot neighbors; the resulting filled graph governs factor storage and arithmetic, subject to pivoting effects.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is sparse and symmetric.
\(PHP^{\mathsf T}=LL^{\mathsf T}\) is computed without structural dropping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The filled elimination graph determines the structural pattern of \(L\), while pivot changes may enlarge that pattern.

notation.meaning: number of structural nonzeros in the factor

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property role fits Fill-In Control, and the filled-graph characterization is mathematically standard. An authoritative sparse-factorization locator is required, particularly for the work proxy, amalgamation statement, and effect of unrestricted stability pivoting.

children.title: Dense-Column Handling
children.top_down_role: Special treatment of columns that would otherwise cause extensive fill.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Setup and per-right-hand-side work after separating dense columns from a sparse normal matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H_s+UCU^{\mathsf T}\), where \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times k}\), and suppose a factorization of \(H_s\) is available. Set \(W=H_s^{-1}U\) and \(S=C^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}W\). If one solve with \(H_s\) costs \(T_s\), setup costs \(kT_s+O(mk^2+k^3)\) arithmetic for dense \(U\), including formation and factorization of \(S\). Thereafter, \(Hx=b\) is solved by \(z=H_s^{-1}b\), \(Sq=U^{\mathsf T}z\), and \(x=z-Wq\), costing \(T_s+O(mk+k^2)\) per right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense-column separation requires k setup solves and a dense correction of order k; each later right-hand side uses one sparse solve and one small dense solve.
assumptions_latex: \(H_s\), \(C\), and \(S=C^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}H_s^{-1}U\) are nonsingular.
A factorization of \(H_s\) is available.
\(U\) is treated as a dense \(m\times k\) block for the displayed arithmetic bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{setup}}=kT_s+O(mk^2+k^3),\qquad T_{\mathrm{rhs}}=T_s+O(mk+k^2).

notation.meaning: matrix obtained by solving the sparse system against the dense-column block
cost of one solve using the available factorization of the sparse block

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Dense-Column Correction Work
Dense-Column Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Low-rank separation of dense columns in normal equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition \(A=[A_s\;A_d]\) and \(D^2=\operatorname{diag}(D_s^2,D_d^2)\), where \(A_d\) contains \(k\) dense columns. Then
\[AD^2A^{\mathsf T}=H_s+UC U^{\mathsf T},\qquad H_s=A_sD_s^2A_s^{\mathsf T},\quad U=A_d,\quad C=D_d^2.\]
If \(H_s\) and \(C\) are nonsingular, the inverse action is
\[(H_s+UCU^{\mathsf T})^{-1}=H_s^{-1}-H_s^{-1}U(C^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}H_s^{-1}U)^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}H_s^{-1}.\]
Thus sparse factorization of \(H_s\) is combined with a dense \(k\times k\) correction, avoiding direct fill caused by the dense columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense columns are separated as a low-rank normal-equation correction, combining a sparse factorization with a small dense solve.
assumptions_latex: \(H_s\) and \(C\) are nonsingular.
\(A_d\) contains \(k\) designated dense columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Solves with \(AD^2A^{\mathsf T}\) reduce to solves with \(H_s\) and one dense system of order \(k\).

notation.meaning: sparse and designated dense column blocks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The low-rank representation fits Dense-Column Handling, and the displayed Woodbury formula is consistent with the stated positive diagonal column scaling and nonsingular sparse Gram matrix. A source is required for this treatment as an LP normal-equation fill-control method.

children.title: Structured Factorization Updates
children.top_down_role: Factorization modifications exploiting isolated dense or changing structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp admissibility condition for a symmetric low-rank Cholesky downdate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\succ0\) and \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times k}\). Then \(H_-=H-UU^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) if and only if \(I_k-U^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}U\succ0\), equivalently \(\lVert H^{-1/2}U\rVert_2<1\). If the norm equals one, \(H_-\) is positive semidefinite and singular; if it exceeds one, \(H_-\) is indefinite. In either failure case a positive-definite Cholesky downdate is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank Cholesky downdate remains positive definite exactly when the scaled update has spectral norm below one.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is symmetric positive definite.
The modification has downdate form \(-UU^{\mathsf T}\).
\(H^{-1/2}\) denotes the symmetric positive-definite inverse square root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H-UU^{\mathsf T}\succ0\iff I_k-U^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}U\succ0\iff\lVert H^{-1/2}U\rVert_2<1.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definite Downdate Criterion
Structured Factorization Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of an existing factorization under low-rank changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(H=LL^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) is already factored and the next Newton matrix satisfies \(H_+=H+UCU^{\mathsf T}\), with \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times k}\). When \(C\) and \(C^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}U\) are nonsingular,
\[H_+^{-1}=H^{-1}-H^{-1}U(C^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}U)^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}.\]
Hence a solve with \(H_+\) can reuse triangular solves with \(L\) and factor only a \(k\times k\) correction. For positive semidefinite updates, Cholesky rank updates are admissible; downdates require \(H_+\succ0\) and numerical stability checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank change to a factored Newton matrix can be handled by triangular solves and a small correction, provided definiteness is preserved.
assumptions_latex: \(H=LL^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
\(C^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}U\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed formula reuses the factorization of \(H\) to apply \(H_+^{-1}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits Structured Factorization Updates and the inverse-update formula is standard under the stated nonsingularity conditions. No source supports the factor-reuse method or the admissibility and stability qualifications for Cholesky updates and downdates.

children.title: Primal-Dual Regularization Family

children.title: Primal Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization applied to primal-side local-system structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal stabilization of the scaled primal block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For D\succ0 diagonal and \rho>0, primal regularization replaces \begin{pmatrix}-D^{-2}&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix} by K_\rho=\begin{pmatrix}-(D^{-2}+\rho I)&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}. Eliminating \Delta x gives H_\rho=A(D^{-2}+\rho I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}. The shifted primal block is negative definite and \|(D^{-2}+\rho I)^{-1}\|_2\leq1/\rho. Moreover, H_\rho is positive definite exactly when A has full row rank; primal regularization alone cannot remove Schur-complement singularity caused by row-rank deficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive primal-block shift limits inverse scaling but does not cure constraint row-rank deficiency.
assumptions_latex: D\succ0 is diagonal.
\rho>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H_\rho=A(D^{-2}+\rho I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}, and H_\rho\succ0 if and only if A has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Regularization

children.title: Dual Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization applied to dual-side local-system structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal stabilization of the multiplier block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For D\succ0 diagonal and \delta>0, dual regularization replaces the zero multiplier block by K_\delta=\begin{pmatrix}-D^{-2}&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&\delta I\end{pmatrix}. Eliminating \Delta x produces the shifted Schur complement AD^2A^{\mathsf T}+\delta I, which is positive definite for every A and satisfies \lambda_{\min}(AD^2A^{\mathsf T}+\delta I)\geq\delta. The resulting direction solves the shifted rather than the original Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive dual-block shift makes the Schur complement positive definite even when the constraint matrix is rank deficient.
assumptions_latex: D\succ0 is diagonal.
\delta>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: AD^2A^{\mathsf T}+\delta I\succ0 and \lambda_{\min}(AD^2A^{\mathsf T}+\delta I)\geq\delta.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Regularization

children.title: Coupled Primal-Dual Regularization
children.top_down_role: Joint regularization of primal-dual Newton-system components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous positive diagonal stabilization of both augmented-system blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D\succ0 be diagonal and \rho,\delta>0. Define K_{\rho,\delta}=\begin{pmatrix}-(D^{-2}+\rho I)&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&\delta I\end{pmatrix}. Its diagonal blocks are negative and positive definite, respectively, so it is symmetric quasidefinite and nonsingular for every A. Eliminating \Delta x yields the positive-definite Schur complement A(D^{-2}+\rho I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}+\delta I.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive shifts on both blocks create a nonsingular symmetric quasidefinite augmented system and a positive-definite Schur complement.
assumptions_latex: D\succ0 is diagonal.
\rho>0 and \delta>0.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{\rho,\delta} is nonsingular and A(D^{-2}+\rho I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}+\delta I\succ0 for every A.
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Primal-Dual Regularization

children.title: Regularization Strength Regimes
children.top_down_role: Stability and solution-distortion effects associated with regularization magnitude.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation and residual criteria separating accuracy-preserving and bias-dominated shifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Ku=r with K nonsingular, and let (K+E)u_E=r. If \eta=\|K^{-1}E\|<1, then \frac{\|u_E-u\|}{\|u\|}\leq\frac{\kappa(K)}{1-\eta}\frac{\|E\|}{\|K\|}. Thus a shift is accuracy-preserving relative to a requested direction tolerance when this bound is sufficiently small. Larger shifts may be used for stabilization, but the original-system residual must be checked: Ku_E-r=-Eu_E. A family of shifts is asymptotically bias-free when \|Eu_E\| tends to zero at the required Newton-solve scale; a fixed nonvanishing shift need not have this property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularization is accuracy-preserving only when its perturbation is small enough; larger shifts require residual checks against the unregularized Newton system.
assumptions_latex: K is nonsingular.
All norms are compatible operator and vector norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed bound controls direction perturbation, while Ku_E-r=-Eu_E exactly measures residual bias for the original system.

notation.meaning: Condition number in the chosen operator norm.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Strength Regimes

children.title: Iterative Refinement
children.top_down_role: Residual-correction mechanisms for improving computed Newton directions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-correction refinement of a computed Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a Newton system Ku=r and reusable computed factors represented by a nonsingular operator M, compute u^{(0)} from Mu^{(0)}=r. For j=0,1,\ldots, form e^{(j)}=r-Ku^{(j)}, solve Md^{(j)}=e^{(j)}, and set u^{(j+1)}=u^{(j)}+d^{(j)}. Stop when \|e^{(j)}\|\leq\tau(\|K\|\|u^{(j)}\|+\|r\|), or report the last iterate and residual after the correction limit. Residual evaluation in precision higher than that used for the factors can reduce loss from cancellation and rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse the Newton factors to solve successive residual equations until a normwise backward-error test or correction limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: K is nonsingular when a unique exact Newton direction is required.
M is nonsingular and its computed factors remain usable for correction solves.
The displayed norms are mutually compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful return satisfies the stated normwise backward-error test; otherwise the final residual records failure to attain it.

notation.meaning: Operator represented by the reused computed factors.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Factor Iterative Refinement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Small Residual Does Not Ensure Small Forward Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning boundary for interpreting refinement residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For 0<\varepsilon<1, let K=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon), r=(1,\varepsilon)^{\mathsf T}, u=K^{-1}r=(1,1)^{\mathsf T}, and \widehat u=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}. Then \frac{\|r-K\widehat u\|_2}{\|r\|_2}=\frac{\varepsilon}{\sqrt{1+\varepsilon^2}}\to0, while \frac{\|u-\widehat u\|_2}{\|u\|_2}=1/\sqrt2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrarily small relative residual can coexist with order-one forward error for an ill-conditioned Newton matrix.
assumptions_latex: 0<\varepsilon<1.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A residual test alone is not a forward-accuracy certificate without conditioning information.
knowledge_statements.title: Small Residual Does Not Ensure Small Forward Error

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of exact-arithmetic contraction conclusions in computed refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In floating-point refinement the computed residual and correction contain rounding errors, so the exact recurrence e^{(j+1)}=(I-KM^{-1})e^{(j)} need not hold. Refinement may stagnate once residual-formation or correction-solve errors are comparable to the remaining residual; geometric convergence therefore requires accuracy assumptions beyond q<1 for the ideal operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding errors can stop refinement at an accuracy floor even when the ideal exact-arithmetic iteration is contractive.
assumptions_latex: Residuals and corrections are evaluated in finite precision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact-arithmetic contraction alone does not guarantee indefinite residual reduction in floating point.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Precision Stagnation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence and correction-count bound for fixed-factor refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For exact-arithmetic refinement e^{(j)}=r-Ku^{(j)}, Md^{(j)}=e^{(j)}, and u^{(j+1)}=u^{(j)}+d^{(j)}, one has e^{(j+1)}=(I-KM^{-1})e^{(j)}. Hence, in any subordinate norm, q=\|I-KM^{-1}\|<1 implies \|e^{(j)}\|\leq q^j\|e^{(0)}\| and u^{(j)}\to K^{-1}r. A residual target \|e^{(j)}\|\leq\epsilon is reached after at most \left\lceil\log(\|e^{(0)}\|/\epsilon)/\log(1/q)\right\rceil corrections when \epsilon<\|e^{(0)}\|.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-factor refinement converges geometrically when its residual-propagation operator is a contraction.
assumptions_latex: K and M are nonsingular.
Residual formation, correction solves, and updates are exact.
q=\|I-KM^{-1}\|<1 in a subordinate norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|e^{(j)}\|\leq q^j\|e^{(0)}\|, with the displayed logarithmic correction bound.

notation.meaning: Contraction factor of the residual-propagation operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Arithmetic Refinement Contraction
Iterative Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-correction iteration for a computed Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a nonsingular Newton matrix \(K\), right-hand side \(r\), an available numerical factorization \(M\approx K\), tolerance \(\tau\), and maximum count \(J\), first solve \(Mu^{(0)}=r\). For \(j=0,\ldots,J-1\), compute the residual \(e^{(j)}=r-Ku^{(j)}\), preferably in higher precision. Stop and return \(u^{(j)}\) if \(\lVert e^{(j)}\rVert\leq\tau(\lVert K\rVert\lVert u^{(j)}\rVert+\lVert r\rVert)\). Otherwise solve \(Md^{(j)}=e^{(j)}\) using the same factors and set \(u^{(j+1)}=u^{(j)}+d^{(j)}\). Return the last iterate with its residual if the test is not met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated residual solves reuse the Newton factors to correct the direction until a normwise backward-error test or iteration limit is reached.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is nonsingular.
The factors represented by \(M\) remain usable for correction solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a corrected direction satisfying the backward-error test, or the final iterate accompanied by its residual.

notation.meaning: operator represented by the computed factors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is correct for Iterative Refinement, and the residual-correction loop and backward-error stopping test are coherent. An authoritative locator is required for the algorithm, higher-precision residual recommendation, and stopping criterion.

children.title: Solver-Lifecycle Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Preprocessing, initialization, stopping, and postprocessing surrounding the core interior iteration.

children.title: Presolve-Scaling Lifecycle Interface
children.top_down_role: Redundancy removal, size reduction, sparsification, and numerical equilibration.

children.title: Presolve Reductions
children.top_down_role: Redundancy removal, fixed-variable elimination, and model-size reduction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core exact reductions and immediate infeasibility tests for a bounded equality-form LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ \ell\le x\le u\}\), repeatedly: substitute variables fixed by \(\ell_j=u_j\); solve singleton equality rows and reject an implied value outside its bounds; delete a zero row when its right-hand side is zero and declare infeasibility otherwise; delete an equality row proved to be a consistent linear combination of retained rows; and tighten bounds using sound row-activity intervals. Record substitutions, row dependencies, objective constants, and bound changes needed by postsolve. Each accepted reduction must preserve the feasible set under its reconstruction map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve applies sound fixed-variable, singleton, zero-row, redundant-row, and bound-tightening rules while recording their reversal data.
assumptions_latex: Every algebraic test is exact or uses a separately sound numerical enclosure.
Every eliminating transformation records its required inverse data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The result is an equivalent reduced LP with reconstruction records, or an immediate verified contradiction.
knowledge_statements.title: Elementary Reversible Presolve Reductions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving bound propagation from one equality row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a^\top x=b\) and an index \(j\) with \(a_j\ne0\), compute sound lower and upper bounds on \(\sum_{i\ne j}a_ix_i\) from the current variable bounds using sign-aware endpoint choices. The equality then implies an interval for \(x_j\); intersect it with \([\ell_j,u_j]\). A proper nonempty intersection is valid tightening, while an empty intersection proves that the current bounded row system is infeasible. Floating-point activity bounds must be rounded outward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound row-activity intervals imply tighter bounds, and an empty implied intersection proves infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Activity bounds safely enclose every attainable activity, using outward rounding when computed in floating point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The intersection preserves all feasible points or verifies infeasibility when empty.
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Activity Bound Tightening

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact redundancy or inconsistency test for proportional equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(a_k^\top=\lambda a_i^\top\) with \(\lambda\ne0\), then row \(k\) is redundant when \(b_k=\lambda b_i\), provided its dependence is recorded. If \(b_k\ne\lambda b_i\), the two equalities are inconsistent and certify primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proportional equalities are redundant when their right-hand sides scale consistently and contradictory otherwise.
assumptions_latex: The proportionality and right-hand-side comparison are established exactly or by a sound numerical test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The second row is safely deleted or the row pair verifies infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Proportional Equality-Row Test
Presolve Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reversible equivalence-preserving simplification before interior-point iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the LP \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\;\ell\leq x\leq u\}\), repeatedly apply certified reductions: substitute variables with \(\ell_i=u_i\); solve singleton equalities when their implied values satisfy the bounds; delete zero rows whose right-hand side is zero; declare infeasibility for a zero row with nonzero right-hand side or for a singleton-implied bound violation; and tighten bounds using row activities without removing feasible points. Record every substitution and deletion in a postsolve stack. Output either an infeasibility certificate or a reduced LP with an affine reconstruction map \(x=T\bar x+t\) preserving feasibility and objective values up to a recorded constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve repeatedly applies sound substitutions, row tests, and bound tightening, recording a map that reconstructs solutions of the original LP.
assumptions_latex: \(A,c,b,\ell,u\) are finite-dimensional LP data.
Each applied reduction records the data needed for reversal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns certified infeasibility or an equivalent reduced LP with reconstruction \(x=T\bar x+t\).

notation.meaning: variable vector of the reduced LP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Presolve Reductions, but the claimed certified-infeasibility output and global affine reconstruction guarantee combine several reductions whose certificate and reversibility conditions are not fully specified. A presolve source is needed before the mathematical scope and guarantees can be trusted.

children.title: Sparsity-Preserving Presolve
children.top_down_role: Presolve transformations designed to retain favorable sparse structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local structural-fill test for an otherwise valid presolve substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(x_j\) occurs in \(p\) retained rows and is solved from a pivot row containing \(q\) other retained variables. Substitution into the other \(p-1\) rows can create at most \((p-1)q\) coefficient positions before accounting for positions already present or exact cancellations. Estimate the net structural additions and recovery-record storage, and perform the substitution only when the declared fill and storage budgets are met; otherwise retain the row and variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparsity-aware presolver estimates substitution fill and retains variables whose elimination would exceed declared structural budgets.
assumptions_latex: The pivot coefficient is nonzero.
The estimate counts structural positions without relying on numerical cancellation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted substitution satisfies the declared local fill and record-storage tests.

notation.meaning: Column incidence and the number of other variables in the pivot row.

knowledge_statements.title: Substitution Fill Safeguard

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint Sparsity Does Not Bound Factor Fill
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between presolved-matrix sparsity and interior-point factorization cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bound on \(\operatorname{nnz}(\widehat A)\) alone does not give a comparable bound on fill in a Cholesky or \(LDL^\top\) factorization of an interior-point normal-equation or augmented-system matrix. Factor fill depends on the associated graph and elimination ordering, and a sparse matrix can have dense factors under an unfavorable ordering. Matrix-level sparsity preservation therefore implies no factorization-memory or arithmetic bound without additional graph and ordering assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping the reduced constraint matrix sparse does not by itself keep interior-point factors sparse.
assumptions_latex: No independent graph-width or elimination-ordering fill bound is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constraint-matrix sparsity alone does not bound factor fill or factorization work.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Sparsity Does Not Bound Factor Fill

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cancellation Is Not a Safe Structural Fill Policy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical boundary for predicting sparse substitutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A substitution that appears sparse only because computed coefficients nearly cancel is not structurally sparsity-preserving: rounding, scaling, or later data changes can leave small nonzeros in all predicted positions. Fill acceptance should therefore use symbolic incidence or a declared numerical-dropping rule whose model error is separately controlled, rather than assuming near cancellation is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near cancellation cannot safely justify a structural no-fill claim unless coefficient dropping and its error are explicitly controlled.
assumptions_latex: Predicted cancellations are numerical rather than exact algebraic identities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Structural fill must be counted before uncontrolled numerical cancellation.
knowledge_statements.title: Cancellation Is Not a Safe Structural Fill Policy
Sparsity-Preserving Presolve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines structural preservation for an LP presolve transformation and its reconstruction maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an LP with constraint matrix \(A\), a presolve transformation is sparsity-preserving with fill budget \(\kappa\geq 1\) if it produces a reduced matrix \(\widehat A\), reversible transformation records, and recovery maps for primal and dual solutions such that \(\operatorname{nnz}(\widehat A)\leq \kappa\operatorname{nnz}(A)\). Every eliminated row, column, or coefficient must be represented by records whose total storage is \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A))\), and applying either recovery map must require \(O(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+m+n)\) arithmetic operations. The reduction may change dimensions but may not introduce an unrecorded dense Schur complement or dense substitution block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolve is sparsity-preserving when reduced data, transformation records, and solution recovery remain linearly sparse and avoid hidden dense substitution structures.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
The presolve reductions are algebraically reversible for retained solution and certificate classes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{nnz}(\widehat A)\leq\kappa\operatorname{nnz}(A)\), with linear-size records and linear-time reconstruction.

notation.meaning: number of stored nonzero entries of A

review_flags: implementation-level definition lacks a supplied presolve reference
exact complexity convention should be source-checked

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fill, record-storage, and reconstruction-time requirements form a plausible implementation-level definition, but no source establishes this particular meaning of sparsity-preserving presolve. The plain statement also omits several exact requirements.

children.title: Data Scaling
children.top_down_role: Numerical equilibration of constraint, variable, and objective data.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reversible row-column coefficient equilibration heuristic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Alternately divide each nonzero row by its largest absolute coefficient and each nonzero column by its largest absolute coefficient, accumulating the positive diagonal factors \(D_r,D_c\). Do not divide zero rows or columns; pass them to presolve diagnostics. Stop after a declared sweep limit or equilibration criterion, and transform \(b,c,x,y,s\) consistently with the accumulated factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating row and column normalization balances coefficient magnitudes while recording reversible diagonal factors.
assumptions_latex: Every divisor used is finite and strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The processed row and column maxima are equilibrated according to the stopping rule, and the transformation remains reversible.
knowledge_statements.title: Alternating Max-Norm Equilibration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural and floating-point limits of numerical equilibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular diagonal \(D_r,D_c\), \(\operatorname{rank}(D_rAD_c)=\operatorname{rank}(A)\) and \((D_rAD_c)_{ij}=0\iff a_{ij}=0\). Thus diagonal scaling cannot remove rank deficiency or structural singularity. Extreme factors can also amplify rounding or cause overflow or underflow, so improved coefficient balance alone does not certify a smaller condition number or greater numerical accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal scaling preserves rank and sparsity, cannot cure structural singularity, and can be harmful when factors are extreme.
assumptions_latex: \(D_r,D_c\) are nonsingular diagonal matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Structural defects persist and numerical improvement is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.title: Limits of Diagonal Scaling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact row-column scaling and inverse coordinate mappings for a standard-form primal-dual LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^\top y:A^\top y+s=c,\ s\ge0\}\), let \(D_r,D_c\) be positive diagonal matrices and define \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\), \(\widehat b=D_rb\), and \(\widehat c=D_cc\). The mappings \(x=D_c\widehat x\), \(y=D_r\widehat y\), and \(s=D_c^{-1}\widehat s\) are bijections between the corresponding primal-dual feasible sets and preserve both objective values and complementarity: \(c^\top x=\widehat c^\top\widehat x\), \(b^\top y=\widehat b^\top\widehat y\), and \(x^\top s=\widehat x^\top\widehat s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal row and column scaling gives an equivalent primal-dual LP with explicit reversible coordinate mappings.
assumptions_latex: \(D_r\) and \(D_c\) are diagonal with finite strictly positive entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility, objectives, optimality, and complementarity correspond exactly under the stated mappings.

notation.meaning: Positive diagonal row and column scaling matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Diagonal Primal-Dual Scaling
Data Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal row-column scaling for equality-form primal-dual LP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal-dual pair \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\). For positive diagonal matrices \(D_r\) and \(D_c\), define \(\widehat A=D_rAD_c\), \(\widehat b=D_rb\), and \(\widehat c=D_cc\). The scaled primal uses \(x=D_c\widehat x\); the scaled dual uses \(y=D_r\widehat y\) and \(s=D_c^{-1}\widehat s\). These substitutions give exact correspondences between feasible points, preserve objective values, and satisfy \(x^Ts=\widehat x^T\widehat s\). Thus diagonal scaling changes numerical magnitudes without changing feasibility, optimality, or complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal row and column scalings produce an equivalent primal-dual LP, with explicit inverse mappings preserving objectives and complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(D_r\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) and \(D_c\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) are diagonal with strictly positive entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and scaled primal-dual feasible sets correspond bijectively and preserve objective values and \(x^Ts\).

notation.meaning: positive diagonal row and column scaling matrices

review_flags: no supplied locator specifically supports the scaling identities

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagonal scaling identities and mappings are mathematically consistent and representation is the correct knowledge kind, but the record supplies no inspectable source.

children.title: Postsolve Reconstruction
children.top_down_role: Transfer of reduced-model solutions back to the original representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse reconstruction and original-model validation after presolve and scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Store every forward transformation together with inverse rules indexed by terminal-object type. Given a reduced primal-dual solution, infeasibility certificate, or feasible-point-plus-ray unboundedness certificate, replay the records in reverse order only when every record supports that object type, restoring eliminated variables, rows, bounds, multipliers, slacks, objective constants, and scaling coordinates. Recompute the defining residuals, sign conditions, objective gap, or ray inequalities from the original data. Transfer the reduced status only if the reconstructed object satisfies its original-model predicate; otherwise return reconstruction failure or an indeterminate status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve reverses typed transformation records and transfers a status only after the reconstructed object passes its original-model test.
assumptions_latex: Original LP data and the ordered transformation log are available.
Every replayed transformation has an inverse rule for the terminal object being reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an original-coordinate validated object or an explicit reconstruction failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Typed Reverse Postsolve Replay

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Solution Recovery Does Not Imply Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary on the information required in a postsolve log.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A log sufficient to reconstruct primal variables need not reconstruct dual multipliers or rays. For example, deleting a redundant equality without recording its linear dependence leaves primal feasible points unchanged, but the deleted row's multiplier contribution cannot in general be assigned from the retained multipliers alone; dual multipliers may also be nonunique. Likewise, a substitution formula for points need not specify the homogeneous mapping required for recession directions. Status transfer is therefore invalid when the log lacks the inverse data required by the relevant object type.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal recovery records alone do not necessarily recover dual multipliers or recession certificates.
assumptions_latex: At least one transformation record omits dependency or homogeneous-direction data needed by the requested terminal object.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful primal reconstruction alone cannot justify transfer of a dual or ray-based status.
knowledge_statements.title: Solution Recovery Does Not Imply Certificate Recovery
Postsolve Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse reconstruction of solutions and certificates after presolve and scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a terminal reduced-space object \(z_k\), where \(z_k\) is an approximate primal-dual solution or an infeasibility or unboundedness certificate, together with ordered transformation records \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\). For \(i=k,k-1,\ldots,1\), apply the recorded inverse rule \(z_{i-1}=T_i^{-1}(z_i)\), restoring eliminated variables, rows, bounds, dual multipliers, and scaling factors according to the object type. Recompute original-space residuals and certificate inequalities from the unreduced data. Output \(z_0\) with its original-space residual measures only if all required inverse rules succeed; otherwise output an indeterminate reconstruction status rather than transferring the reduced-space status unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Postsolve reverses every recorded reduction and scaling, then revalidates the reconstructed solution or certificate against the original LP.
assumptions_latex: Each applied presolve or scaling transformation has a stored inverse rule for the relevant terminal object.
Original LP data remain available for validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a reconstructed and original-space-validated object \(z_0\), or an indeterminate reconstruction status.

notation.meaning: the ith recorded presolve or scaling transformation
solution or certificate after the first i transformations

review_flags: no supplied locator specifically covers postsolve reconstruction
certificate-specific inverse rules require implementation references

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct kind, but the broad requirement to reconstruct multiple certificate classes depends on transformation-specific inverse rules for which no source is supplied.

children.title: Practical Starting-Point Construction
children.top_down_role: Construction of interior or embedded initial iterates in solver implementations.

knowledge_statements.title: Practical Starting-Point Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infeasible-interior initialization for a full-row-rank standard-form primal-dual LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\), \(b\), and \(c\), compute \(\bar x=A^T(AA^T)^{-1}b\), \(\bar y=(AA^T)^{-1}Ac\), and \(\bar s=c-A^T\bar y\). Set \(\delta_x=\max\{-\tfrac32\min_j\bar x_j,0\}\) and \(\delta_s=\max\{-\tfrac32\min_j\bar s_j,0\}\), then form \(x'=\bar x+\delta_xe\) and \(s'=\bar s+\delta_se\). Finally set \(x^0=x'+\tfrac12(x'^Ts')/(e^Ts')e\), \(s^0=s'+\tfrac12(x'^Ts')/(e^Tx')e\), and \(y^0=\bar y\). Output the strictly positive, generally infeasible primal-dual starting point \((x^0,y^0,s^0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-squares primal and dual estimates are shifted and centered to obtain strictly positive initial primal variables and slacks for an infeasible interior-point method, provided the shifted vectors have positive sums and positive inner product.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
The shifted vectors satisfy \(e^Tx'>0\), \(e^Ts'>0\), and \(x'^Ts'>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^0>0\) and \(s^0>0\); primal and dual equality feasibility is not required.

notation.meaning: all-ones vector in the primal variable space
initial primal variable, dual multiplier, and dual slack

source_refs.locator: 6 Infeasible-Interior-Point Algorithms p. 107

review_flags: constants and centering shifts should be checked against the cited initialization formula

source_witnesses.locator: 6 Infeasible-Interior-Point Algorithms p. 107

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal algebraic starting condition for an infeasible-start primal-dual method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the standard-form primal-dual equations, an algebraically interior initialization requires \(x^0>0\) and \(s^0>0\); \(y^0\), \(r_p^0=Ax^0-b\), and \(r_d^0=A^\top y^0+s^0-c\) may be arbitrary finite vectors. This condition makes the point admissible to an infeasible-interior iteration, but it does not by itself establish any method-specific neighborhood or convergence hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible-interior start requires positive primal variables and slacks, not equality feasibility; convergence conditions are separate.
assumptions_latex: All initial components and residuals are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^0>0\) and \(s^0>0\) give an interior start even when \(r_p^0\ne0\) or \(r_d^0\ne0\).

notation.meaning: Initial primal and dual equality residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Admissibility of an Infeasible-Interior Start

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Heuristic initialization for a primal–dual LP method. The explicit inverse requires full row rank of A; the final formulas guarantee strict positivity only under a positive-overlap condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume AA^T\text{ is invertible}. Set \tilde x=A^T(AA^T)^{-1}b,\ \tilde\lambda=(AA^T)^{-1}Ac,\ \tilde s=c-A^T\tilde\lambda. Define \delta_x=\max\{-\tfrac32\min_i\tilde x_i,0\},\ \delta_s=\max\{-\tfrac32\min_i\tilde s_i,0\},\ \hat x=\tilde x+\delta_xe,\ \hat s=\tilde s+\delta_se. When e^T\hat x>0 and e^T\hat s>0, set \hat\delta_x=\tfrac12\frac{\hat x^T\hat s}{e^T\hat s},\ \hat\delta_s=\tfrac12\frac{\hat x^T\hat s}{e^T\hat x}, and x^0=\hat x+\hat\delta_xe,\ \lambda^0=\tilde\lambda,\ s^0=\hat s+\hat\delta_se.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the minimum-norm primal equality solution and the dual equality solution whose slack has minimum norm. Uniform shifts make the primal vector and slack nonnegative; complementarity-weighted offsets then move them away from zero and reduce scale imbalance. The construction costs about one primal–dual step. If the shifted vectors have zero complementarity, the displayed offsets do not guarantee a strictly positive starting point.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\qquad AA^T\text{ is invertible}.
e^T\hat x>0,\qquad e^T\hat s>0\quad\text{for the offset formulas}.
\hat x^T\hat s>0\quad\text{for the strict-positivity conclusion}.

children.title: Optimality Termination Tests

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Termination Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized approximate KKT test for a standard-form primal-dual LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate \((x,y,s)\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), define \(r_p=Ax-b\), \(r_d=A^Ty+s-c\), and \(g=c^Tx-b^Ty\). Declare approximate optimality only if \(x\geq-\varepsilon e\), \(s\geq-\varepsilon e\), \(\|r_p\|/(1+\|b\|)\leq\varepsilon\), \(\|r_d\|/(1+\|c\|)\leq\varepsilon\), and \(|g|/(1+|c^Tx|+|b^Ty|)\leq\varepsilon\). The norm and tolerance must be fixed by the solver interface. Passing only the complementarity or objective-gap test is insufficient when either feasibility residual fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate optimality requires primal feasibility, dual feasibility, sign bounds, and a normalized duality-gap test to pass simultaneously.
assumptions_latex: The primal is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and the dual is \(\max\{b^Ty:A^Ty+s=c,\ s\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All displayed normalized KKT tests imply the solver may return approximate-optimal status at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

children.title: Feasibility Termination Tests

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Termination Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate normalized tests for approximate primal and dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the standard-form primal-dual pair and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), a candidate \(x\) is approximately primal feasible if \(\|Ax-b\|/(1+\|b\|)\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\|\min(x,0)\|/(1+\|x\|)\leq\varepsilon\). A candidate \((y,s)\) is approximately dual feasible if \(\|A^Ty+s-c\|/(1+\|c\|)\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\|\min(s,0)\|/(1+\|s\|)\leq\varepsilon\), where componentwise minima are used. These tests establish feasibility status only; without an objective-gap or complementarity test they do not establish optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalized equality residuals and violations of nonnegativity determine approximate primal and dual feasibility, independently of optimality.
assumptions_latex: The primal and dual use equality form with nonnegative \(x\) and \(s\).
A norm and tolerance \(\varepsilon\) are fixed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicates define approximate primal and dual feasibility at tolerance \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Status Tests
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for infeasibility of an equality-form primal LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), a vector \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) certifies primal infeasibility when \(A^Ty\leq0\) and \(b^Ty>0\). A numerical solver may report certified infeasibility only after normalizing nonzero \(y\) and verifying both inequalities against stated tolerances in the original, unscaled problem. Failure to find such a vector does not certify feasibility and must not itself trigger an infeasible status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized Farkas vector with nonpositive transpose image and positive right-hand-side pairing certifies primal infeasibility; absence of one proves nothing.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
Certificate inequalities are rechecked using original-space data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of \(y\) with \(A^Ty\leq0\) and \(b^Ty>0\) implies \(P=\varnothing\).

children.title: Indeterminate Status Handling
children.top_down_role: Solver outcomes lacking sufficiently reliable status evidence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status boundary separating a solver stopping reason from a validated mathematical LP status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a run terminates without an output satisfying a declared optimality predicate and without a validated infeasibility or unboundedness certificate in original coordinates, its mathematical LP status is indeterminate. An iteration, time, memory, stagnation, or numerical-failure limit is only a stopping reason and does not itself imply optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness. Conflicting candidate statuses or failed original-space validation likewise leave the status indeterminate until one definitive predicate is validated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stopping reason is not a mathematical LP status; absent consistent original-space evidence for a definitive status, the outcome remains indeterminate.
assumptions_latex: Definitive statuses are assigned only through declared predicates checked in original coordinates.
